# Environment variable reference

Every environment variable that the Ace Combat Zero recompilation runtime (`build/zero/ac5.exe`, built from `runtime/`) and the launcher scripts at the repository root read, collected from the source on @@DATE@@. Line numbers point at the place where each variable is read and will drift as the code changes.

## How the variables are used

Every switch below is read from the process environment, almost always once (on first use) and then cached, so a change needs a restart. Export the variables in Git Bash before starting `build/zero/ac5.exe`, put them in front of a single command, or let `play_zero_vr.sh` set the common ones from its mode words. `play_zero_vr.sh` keeps a value you exported for the variables it writes as `${VAR:-default}` (`PS2_UPSCALE` outside the sharp mode, `PS2_XR_RUNTIME`, `PS2_FIELD_HZ`, `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL`). It always overwrites `PS2_XR`, `PS2_XR_MODE`, `ACZ_VR_HEADLOOK` (stick mode) and `PS2_XR_MULTIVIEW` (sharp mode). Anything else you export passes straight through to the game.

**The ENHANCEMENTS settings (bug #64, 2026-10-23).** The player-facing improvements are also settings: the pause menu's ENHANCEMENTS page (View + Menu > X in the menus between missions, F4 > Enhancements on the window) saves them to `build/zero/ac5_settings.ini` (`[enhancements]`, plus the existing `[immersion]`, `[graphics] realistic_terrain` and `[input] pad_layout`). With `ACZ_MENU_SETTINGS=1`, which `play_zero_vr.sh` exports, the runtime sets each item's switch from the file at start-up (before anything reads it) unless the switch is already in the environment: a variable set by hand or by a launcher word wins for that session and the page shows it locked. Test scripts (`run_test.sh` & co.) do not set `ACZ_MENU_SETTINGS`, so their switches keep the built-in defaults listed below, whatever the user's file says. The rows, their keys, switches, defaults and when a change takes effect, the three layers (the launcher before the game, ACZ_LAUNCHER; the page; the expert keys of the file, listed by F4 > Enhancements > Expert (ini)) and the migration of the old keys: `docs/SETTINGS.md`; the table is `runtime/src/ps2_settings.c` (`enh_rows`, `enh_combo_tab`). A page row can stand for several switches (K_COMBO: EDGE SMOOTHING, TERRAIN LOOK, BUILDINGS ...): the switches below stay as they are; only the file has one key for them.

```bash
cd <the repository>

# through the launcher (VR, mission 1 straight away, native renderer, in-between frames)
./play_zero_vr.sh sharp m1 native smooth

# one-off extra variables for a single launcher run
PS2_SPEED_LOG=1 PS2_XR_DUMP_EYES=1200 ./play_zero_vr.sh m1

# by hand, without the launcher
export PS2_XR=1 PS2_XR_MODE=stereo PS2_UPSCALE=3 ACZ_BOOT_MISSION=1
ISO=<your disc image>
build/zero/ac5.exe --data gen_zero --disc "$(cygpath -w "$ISO")" --watchdog 0 > zero_play.log 2>&1

# exported variables stay set in that shell: clear them all before an unrelated test
unset $(compgen -v | grep -E '^(PS2|ACZ)_')
```

### How values are parsed

- **Presence flags** (written as `any` in the Values column): the variable only has to exist. `getenv(...) != NULL` checks and the `PS2_ENV()` macro (`runtime/include/ps2_runtime.h`) treat `VAR=0` as on too, so unset these to turn them off.
- **Default-on switches** (`0` in the Values column): the feature is on unless the value starts with `0`.
- **Opt-in switches** (`1`): only a value starting with `1` turns them on (some accept any value that does not start with `0`; those rows say "non-0").
- Numbers go through `atoi`/`atof`/`strtol(..., 0)`, so `0x` hex works where the code uses `strtol`/`strtoul` with base 0. The float parsers in `zero_vr.c` and `ps2_xr.c` (`env_float`, `envf`) accept `.` or `,` as the decimal separator.
- Tags at the start of Meaning: **[debug]** diagnostic or inspection aid, **[experimental]** opt-in feature still being evaluated, **[AC5]** only does something on Ace Combat 5 (SLUS-20851); on Zero the code checks fail and the runtime logs that it is off.

### Most useful day to day

| Variable | Typical value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `PS2_XR` + `PS2_XR_MODE` | `1` + `stereo` | VR on, synchronous stereo (`mono`, `cinema` also exist) |
| `PS2_XR_RUNTIME` | Meta `oculus_openxr_64.json` | Pick the OpenXR runtime (the launcher uses Meta's when it is installed, else the system's active one) |
| `ACZ_DISC` | your disc image or folder | The disc for the launcher and the scripted runs |
| `PS2_UPSCALE` | `2`-`4` | Internal resolution: the main sharpness/GPU cost knob |
| `ACZ_BOOT_MISSION` | `1`..`18` | Boot straight into a campaign mission, flying ~15 s after launch |
| `PS2_RN_VP` | `1` | Native renderer for models and terrain (needed by the cockpit lighting and the smooth mode's object motion) |
| `PS2_XR_RERENDER` | `1` | Draw in-between frames at the headset rate (launcher word `smooth`) |
| `PS2_XR_MULTIVIEW` | `1` | Both eyes in one pass (launcher mode `sharp`) |
| `ACZ_VR_HEADLOOK` | `stick` | Head turns drive the game's look camera outside the cockpit |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL` | `cockpits/f5e_t38.cpit` | 3D stereo cockpit in the R3 view (launcher word `cockpit`) |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_SCALE` | `1.0`-`1.3` | HUD size (1 = original angular size) |
| `ACZ_VR_STEREO_SCALE` | `1.0` | Strength of the stereo depth |
| `PS2_FIELD_HZ` | `60` | 60.00 Hz fields so frames line up with a 120 Hz headset |
| `PS2_SPEED_LOG` | `1` | CPU/GPU timing windows every 5 s in the log |
| `PS2_SHOT_EVERY` / `_FROM` / `_MAX` | `600` / `1200` / `2` | Periodic screenshots to `out/shot_*.ppm` |
| `PS2_XR_DUMP_EYES` | field number | Write the exact left/right images the headset gets |
| `PS2_PAD_SCRIPT` | `"400:START 900:CROSS"` | Scripted button presses for unattended runs |
| `PS2_XR_TEST_HEAD` | `30,10` | Fake head turn (yaw, pitch) when testing without moving the headset |

## Launcher and boot

The debug boot (`ACZ_BOOT_*`) lives in `runtime/src/zero_vr.c` and only works on Ace Combat Zero NTSC-U (SLUS-21346): it checks the game code first and logs `zero-boot: code mismatch` otherwise. Campaign progress after a debug boot is not what a real save would hold.

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACZ_BOOT_MISSION` | unset (normal boot) | `1`..`18` | [debug] Boot straight into campaign mission n, skipping logos, title, menus, movie and briefing | @@ACZ_BOOT_MISSION@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_BRANCH` | `0` | `0`..`2` | Branch of a mission with a choice (04/08/14 operation, 03/10/16 ace variant) | @@ACZ_BOOT_BRANCH@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_DIFF` | `2` (Normal) | `0`..`5` | Difficulty the debug boot writes into the save slot | @@ACZ_BOOT_DIFF@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_STAGE` | from the mission table (mission 1 = stage 0) | stage id (hex ok) | Override the stage id written at GameControl::enter | @@ACZ_BOOT_STAGE@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_AIRCRAFT` | `15` (F-5E) | aircraft id `0`..`35` | Player aircraft for the debug boot (ignored with `ACZ_BOOT_HANGAR=1`) | @@ACZ_BOOT_AIRCRAFT@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_WINGMAN` | `5` (Pixy's F-15C) | aircraft id (`10` = PJ's F-16C) | Wingman aircraft for the debug boot | @@ACZ_BOOT_WINGMAN@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_HANGAR` | off | `1` | Stop at the hangar (aircraft select) instead of going straight to flight | @@ACZ_BOOT_HANGAR@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_SKIP` | `774` | fields; `0` keeps the intro | Press Start this many fields after the mission starts loading, skipping the in-engine intro flyby -- only while the game offers a skip then (bug #99, 2026-10-23): the intro plays (the pad player's update 0x231808 has not run), a mission-start cutscene holds the camera (player flag 0x2000) or the take-off runs (player flag 0x1000, "PRESS START BUTTON TO SKIP"); with the player flying already (M4: from field 154) or a menu up nothing is pressed (the press opened the pause menu over M4's flight at field 805); logged `zero-boot: intro skip due at field ...` | @@ACZ_BOOT_SKIP@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_SKIP_CHECK` | on | `0` | ACZ_BOOT_SKIP presses Start only when the game offers a skip (an intro, a mission-start cutscene, the take-off); `0` = at the field whatever plays (before 2026-10-23) | @@ACZ_BOOT_SKIP_CHECK@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_MOVIES` | off | `1` | [debug] With ACZ_BOOT_MISSION: keep the mission's sequence -- its story movies, mission title and briefing play as in the campaign (then the briefing waits for the pad). Mission 11, a fresh save: MOVIEUS 3, 9, 14, 15, 20, BRIEF 10 (the 2026-10-28 campaign played 3, 11, 12, 17, 18) | @@ACZ_BOOT_MOVIES@@ |
| `ACZ_BOOT_SAVE_POKE` | off | `off:val[:bytes],...` (hex ok; bytes 1, 2 or 4, default 4) | [debug] (fx_mpbm 2026-10-31) Values written into the save slot together with the debug boot's aircraft (the hangar's choices the boot skips): `0x25C:1` with `ACZ_BOOT_AIRCRAFT=35` gives the Morgan its second special weapon, MPBM (8 rounds; the weapon block shows `MPBM`), instead of TLS. 0x28A548 hands the hangar record +0x254, +0x25C, +0x260 and three bytes per aircraft at +0x1E0 + 3 x id to the player's set-up; logged `zero-boot: save slot +0x...` | @@ACZ_BOOT_SAVE_POKE@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_SCENES` | off | any | [debug] Log every scene change (factory, caller, depth, field) and the mission fields at flight start | @@ACZ_DEBUG_SCENES@@ |
| `ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON` | off | `"EVENT[#N]+FIELDS:BUTTON[*K/S] ..."`, `BUTTON` also `AXIS=V` / `AXIS=off` (LX LY RX RY) | [test] (rq3_phases 2026-11-11; in the `PS2_RQ_SUPPORT` builds -- the Quest and the simulator -- since rq17_menus 2026-11-16, the PC objects unchanged; `DUMP` through ps2_vk.h PS2_RQ_DUMPAT_WANT; the menus walk `a private script`) Pad presses timed from the game's phases instead of fixed fields (a BUTTON may also be `SCREEN=N`, rq19_sparkle: the cinema screen's image of the next N screen frames as PS2_XR_DUMP_SCREEN writes it, the render target's region only), for unattended runs through every phase on a device whose loads are slower (PS2_PAD_SCRIPT's fields shift there). EVENT: a scene that starts (its factory is called: `MoviePlay` `MissionTitle` `BriefingMovie` `Briefing` `CampaignSelect` `AircraftSelect` `GameSeqReturnGame` `GameControl` `Debrief` `MainSelect` ..., each logged `test pad: scene X starts`), `enter` / `exit` (GameControl::enter / exit), the phase lines `intro` / `event` / `menu` / `flight` ("mission intro: static screen", "a mission event holds the camera", "menu over the flight", "flight resumed: head tracking on"; `flight` also when head tracking engages in flight: a mission without an intro), `engaged` (head tracking engaged), `dead` (the player's aircraft destroyed: a crash or a shoot-down; logged `test pad: the player's aircraft destroyed`), `fly` (the HUD manager runs for the first time in the mission or again after a stop: the player has control; logged `test pad: the player flies`), `pause` (the in-mission pause menu shows; logged `test pad: the pause menu shows`), `boot`. Prefer `fly` / `pause` to the phase lines: those misfire in the second mission of a session. `#N`: only its N-th time (scenes, `enter`, `exit`, `boot` counted in the session; `intro` `event` `menu` `flight` `engaged` `dead` `fly` `pause` within the mission, from its GameControl::enter), else every time. `+FIELDS`: vblank fields after it. A press is held 8 fields; `*K/S` = K presses S fields apart (S >= 12). `AXIS=V` holds that stick value (LY 0 = stick forward) over PS2_PAD_STICK and ACZ_DEBUG_CFIELD_STEER until changed. `STEER=n` sets the test autopilot's mode from then on (0 off, 1 clouds, 2 circling, 3 a dive, wings level and 50 deg nose down, into the ground: the scripted mission end), back to ACZ_DEBUG_CFIELD_STEER's own at the next GameControl::enter. `DUMP` writes one eye dump (`out/eye_<field>_L/_R.ppm`, as PS2_XR_DUMP_EYES, with `_sc` under PS2_XR_DUMP_SWAPCHAIN) at the next stereo frame: a dump per phase whatever field it comes at. A newer scene drops the presses still pending and releases the held axes, so a confirm repeated until the screen changes never reaches the next screen. Logged `test pad: ...`; scripts for the device: `a private script` | @@ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON@@ |
| `ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON_FILE` | off | file path | [test] (rq17_menus 2026-11-16; `PS2_RQ_SUPPORT` builds) More ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON entries from a file, after the variable's own: one walk through the menus pushed to the device as a file (`a private script` / `menus_b.txt`; step1.sh's rows split their variables at commas and spaces). Line breaks separate entries like spaces; a `#` at the start of a line or after a space or tab starts a comment (an entry's own `#N` follows its event directly). Up to 384 entries in all (was 128). With either variable set the presses also reach our ENHANCEMENTS page and TOUCH CONTROLS card while they are up (ps2_vk.h PS2_RQ_PAGE_FEED; the page reads the host pad, not the game's), and a press that began there stays away from the game until it ends; `AfterDebrief` is one more scene event (the factory 0x282C68 the Debrief names as its successor). A `DEBRIEF` action (`EVENT+FIELDS:DEBRIEF`) arms ACZ_DEBUG_MODE_JUMP=281C38:282BB8 at that moment: the next setNext(MainSelect) -- a failed mission's QUIT MISSION > YES -- opens the game's debriefing instead (in a normal boot the boot-time jump is taken by the title's own setNext(MainSelect)). Logged `test pad: ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON_FILE ...: read` | @@ACZ_TEST_PAD_ON_FILE@@ |
| `PS2_SAVE_DIR` | `saves` | directory | Where the virtual memory cards live (`cardN.ps2mc`) | @@PS2_SAVE_DIR@@ |
| `PS2_SETTINGS_FILE` | `<exe dir>/ac5_settings.ini` | path | Settings file of the F4 menu and the ENHANCEMENTS page (gsreplay only uses a file when this is set) | @@PS2_SETTINGS_FILE@@ |
| `PS2_UI_OPEN` | closed | tab `0`..`8` | Open the F4 settings menu at start on that tab (0 Quick, 1 Display, 2 Rendering, 3 Post, 4 Keyboard, 5 Controller, 6 Analog, 7 Clouds A/B, 8 Enhancements) | @@PS2_UI_OPEN@@ |
| `PS2_UI_TEST` | off | words: `expert`, `tall`, `scroll=N`, `set=KEY:CHOICE`, `reset_ask` | [test] (menu_1105a, for window dumps with PS2_XR_DUMP_SCREEN: `scr_*_win.ppm` has the F4 menu) F4 > Enhancements > Expert (ini) open; the menu as tall as the window; the open tab scrolled to N pixels; a row set as a mouse would when the tab first shows (menu_1105b); F4 > Enhancements' RESET ALL opens its question, nothing is reset (2026-11-05) | @@PS2_UI_TEST@@ |

### Variables only the scripts read

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_UPSCALE_SHARP` | unset (the ENHANCEMENTS RESOLUTION, 4X) | `1`..`8` | `play_zero_vr.sh sharp`: the `PS2_UPSCALE` used together with multiview for this session, over the menu's RESOLUTION | @@LINE:play_zero_vr.sh:PS2_UPSCALE_SHARP:-@@ |
| `REPEAT` | `4` | count | `bench_flat.sh`: how often each field is drawn, passed on as `PS2_BENCH_REPEAT` | @@LINE:bench_flat.sh:rep=${REPEAT@@ |
| `EXTRA_PAD` | empty | `"field:BUTTON ..."` | `run_zero_mission.sh` / `run_zero_soak.sh`: extra entries appended to their `PS2_PAD_SCRIPT` | @@LINE:run_zero_mission.sh:EXTRA_PAD:-@@ |
| `ACZ_EXE` | `build/zero/ac5.exe` | path | `run_zero_mission.sh` / `run_zero_soak.sh`: the executable to run | @@LINE:run_zero_mission.sh:ACZ_EXE:-@@ |

`sweep_missions.sh` and `bench_flat.sh` read no variables of their own; they set runtime variables per run (`sweep_missions.sh`: `ACZ_BOOT_MISSION`, `PS2_RN_VP=1`, `PS2_UPSCALE=2`, `PS2_SPEED_LOG=1`, `PS2_SHOT_EVERY=600`, `PS2_SHOT_FROM=1200`, `PS2_SHOT_MAX=2`; `bench_flat.sh`: `ACZ_BOOT_MISSION=1`, `PS2_UPSCALE`, `PS2_SPEED_LOG=1`, `PS2_BENCH_REPEAT`, and it unsets `PS2_XR`, `PS2_XR_MODE` and `PS2_RN_VP` first). Extra `VAR=value` arguments to `bench_flat.sh`, `run_zero_mission.sh` and `run_zero_soak.sh` are exported before the run.

### What `play_zero_vr.sh` sets

| Launcher word | Variables it sets |
|---|---|
| (always) | `ACZ_LAUNCHER=${ACZ_LAUNCHER:-0}` (the launcher window stays off in this script; the public tree's copy says 1), `ACZ_MENU_SETTINGS=${ACZ_MENU_SETTINGS:-1}` (the ENHANCEMENTS settings apply; among their defaults the HUD scale 1.3, edge AA, LOD bias 2, terrain detail 2, smooth motion, 4x in the sharp mode, the modern pad layout), `SDL_JOYSTICK_ALLOW_BACKGROUND_EVENTS=1`; `PS2_UPSCALE=${PS2_UPSCALE:-3}` in every mode but sharp |
| `stick` (default mode) | `ACZ_VR_HEADLOOK=stick`, then as `stereo` |
| `stereo`, `mono`, `cinema` | `PS2_XR=1`, `PS2_XR_MODE=<mode>`, `PS2_XR_RUNTIME=${PS2_XR_RUNTIME:-<Meta runtime json>}`, `PS2_FIELD_HZ=${PS2_FIELD_HZ:-60}` |
| `sharp` | `PS2_XR_MULTIVIEW=1`, `PS2_UPSCALE=$PS2_UPSCALE_SHARP` only when that is set (else the menu's RESOLUTION, 4X), then as `stick` |
| `flat` | no XR variables |
| `m1` .. `m18` | `ACZ_BOOT_MISSION=<n>` |
| `native` | `PS2_RN_VP=1` |
| `smooth` | `PS2_XR_RERENDER=1` (without the word: the menu's SMOOTH MOTION, on) |
| `modern`, `classic` | `ACZ_PAD_LAYOUT=<word>` (without either: the menu's CONTROLLER LAYOUT, modern) |
| `cockpit` | `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL=${ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL:-cockpits/f5e_t38.cpit}` and the per-aircraft `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODELS` (the menu's 3D COCKPIT OFF drops both at start-up) |

`play_zero_desktop.sh` (the desktop shortcuts) runs `play_zero_vr.sh sharp native cockpit` with `PS2_TEX_STATS=600 PS2_SPEED_LOG=1`; its words: `nosmooth` = `PS2_XR_RERENDER=0`, `clouds3d` = `ACZ_VR_CLOUDS=all` (both over the menu for that session), `record` (OBS recording, scene by `ACZ_REC_SCENE`; tools/playtest/README.md), `clean` (= `record` with `ACZ_REC_CLEAN=1` and `PS2_PASS_MASK=copy` unless set: the recording without the HUD, collection and profile "ACZ VR clean"; wish #236), `cine` (= `record` with `ACZ_REC_CINE=1 ACZ_REC_CINE_WINDOW=2560x1440` unless set: the window's own steady 16:9 view for a trailer, collection and profile "ACZ VR cine"; wish #245; since 2026-11-02 with the frame-exact master by the game itself: `ACZ_REC_EXACT=1` into `~/Videos/ACZ_playtest/acz_cine_<date>_<time>.mkv`, `ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN=game` unless set, OBS with the light profile "ACZ VR cine ref" (voice, game, 960x540 reference, `acz_cineobs_*`) whose Voice track `tools/playtest/recmux.py` copies into the master; bug #264), `noexact` with `cine` (OBS records the picture as before, `ACZ_REC_EXACT=0`), `1080` / `1440` / `4k` with `cine` (= `ACZ_REC_CINE_SCALE` of that height unless set: the view drawn natively at that density; default `1`, the eyes'), `timeline` (= `ACZ_PLAY_TIMELINE=1`: the per-frame timeline CSVs beside the log), `72hz` / `80hz` / `90hz` / `120hz` (= `PS2_XR_REFRESH_HZ`: ask the runtime for that rate; weaker PCs set it in the Link / Virtual Desktop app, README), `m1`..`m18`. Until 2026-10-23 it also exported `PS2_EDGE_AA=1 ACZ_LOD_BIAS=2 ACZ_TERRAIN_DETAIL=2` and the words `smooth modern`: these are now the ENHANCEMENTS defaults (the same environment reaches the game: bug #64).

## VR / XR core

OpenXR session, stereo rendering and head tracking (`runtime/src/ps2_xr.c`, the stereo parts of `runtime/src/ps2_video.c`, and the Zero camera hooks in `runtime/src/zero_vr.c`). Head tracking only engages on the 640x480 flight camera and needs `PS2_XR=1` with `PS2_XR_MODE=mono` or a `stereo` mode.

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_XR` | off | `1` | Turn OpenXR on (only the value `1` counts) | @@PS2_XR@@ |
| `PS2_XR_MODE` | `cinema` | `stereo`, `stereo-alt`, `mono`, `cinema` (anything else = cinema) | stereo: game renders once, the renderer draws each eye with parallax; stereo-alt: eyes alternate per game frame; mono: tracked, no stereo; cinema: virtual screen | @@PS2_XR_MODE@@ |
| `PS2_XR_RUNTIME` | system default OpenXR runtime | path to a runtime `.json` | Copied into `XR_RUNTIME_JSON` before the OpenXR instance is created | @@PS2_XR_RUNTIME@@ |
| `PS2_XR_MULTIVIEW` | off | `1` (needs `PS2_XR=1` and a stereo mode) | [experimental] Both eyes in one pass with Vulkan multiview (2-layer render targets) | @@PS2_XR_MULTIVIEW@@ |
| `PS2_XR_RERENDER` | off (ENHANCEMENTS SMOOTH MOTION: on) | `1` | [experimental] When the headset wants a frame and the game has none, redraw the last one from the extrapolated camera | @@PS2_XR_RERENDER@@ |
| `PS2_XR_REPROJ_NEAR` | `200` | game units; `0` = no limit | In-between frames: GS-path draws with a vertex nearer than this (~33 m) are not extrapolated | @@PS2_XR_REPROJ_NEAR@@ |
| `PS2_XR_REPROJ_GS` | on | `0` | In-between frames: `0` stops reprojecting GS-path geometry | @@PS2_XR_REPROJ_GS@@ |
| `PS2_XR_REPROJ_UNMATCHED` | on | `0` | In-between frames: `0` stops extrapolating native mesh objects with no match in the previous game frame | @@PS2_XR_REPROJ_UNMATCHED@@ |
| `PS2_XR_FROM_RT` | on | `0` | Head-tracked frames go to the headset straight from the render target; `0` uses the window image | @@PS2_XR_FROM_RT@@ |
| `PS2_XR_SCREEN_FROM_RT` | on | `0` | The cinema screen (menus, briefings, story movies, the static screen over the flight, the intro flyby; bug #107, 2026-10-24) is copied from the render target's display region at internal resolution into its own swapchain (0) instead of the window image: at 4x 1792 lines over the screen's 48.5 deg (37 px/deg) instead of the window's 1009 (20.8 px/deg, 56 %); the same region (the window's crop, the movies' own letterbox) on the same 4:3 quad. Same-frame headset simulation (25 px/deg, one bilinear sample, ev in a private script): PSNR to the ideal +2.6..+8.1 dB, vertical edge contrast x1.05-1.10 menus, x1.01-1.10 story movie, x1.05-1.28 briefing (upscaled BRIEF.PAC), x1.22-1.24 pause menu over the flight. The window image stays for an overlay composite, a blank display, a display taller than 512 lines (one field at a movie start) and while the F4 menu is open; not carried over (as in flight): the window's present filter / [postfx] and the F4 FPS counter. GPU (in-run PS2_XR_SCREEN_FROM_RT_AB=30, 4x, 2 runs): the copy +0.008 ms (2048x1792, 14 MB) / +0.013..+0.015 ms (2560x1792, 17.5 MB) per screen frame; swapchain 0 2560x2048 x 3 images (60 MB). `0` = the window image (before 2026-10-24) | @@PS2_XR_SCREEN_FROM_RT@@ |
| `PS2_XR_SCREEN_FROM_RT_AB` | off | N frames | [test] Screen frames alternate N-frame blocks between the render target and the window image; `xr-screen-ab:` GPU ms of the frame's tail (window present + headset copy + prompt layer) and of the whole frame per source every 40 x N screen frames (the first 2 frames of a block not counted) | @@PS2_XR_SCREEN_FROM_RT_AB@@ |
| `PS2_XR_EYE_CROP` | on | `0` | Submit each eye as the crop of the symmetric image that covers its own asymmetric FOV; `0` submits the full image | @@PS2_XR_EYE_CROP@@ |
| `PS2_XR_VIS_MASK` | on (when the runtime offers it) | `0` | XR_KHR_visibility_mask (ov_passes 2026-10-25): the runtime's per-eye hidden-area and visible-area meshes (the lens corners no eye sees) are queried after the session starts and after its change event, checked against the eye's FOV (a mesh whose vertices are not tangents within 1.25 x the FOV is refused and logged), and used by PS2_PASS_MASK. At the first flight frame after a mission start, a RETRY or a jump of the aircraft (the canopy reset's count) it starts afresh at level 0 (fresh window, hold x1, 2 s without action; measured savings kept). Before: M2's take-off clearance (head-tracked stereo, no cockpit; 9.6 ms GPU at 4x in ov_hitch's census, 4.0 ms on the 2026-10-25 build, so on the headset's 6.67-ms budget at x1.2-1.75) raised it to level 3, and the 15-s hold carried the painted sea, no edge AA and the 2-sample cockpit into the first 15 s of flight (simulator with ACZ_VR_GOV_LOAD_X=3.2: level 3 at the flight start, level 0 only 26 s into it; now level 0 throughout; a forced x5.5 load in flight still climbs to 3 in 4.4 s). `0` = every timed frame counts (before) | @@ACZ_VR_GOV_INTRO@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_GOV_OFFRT` | `auto` | `auto`, `0`, comma list of target slots | Governor lever `offrt` (nx_offscreen 2026-10-25, level 3 of the default ACZ_VR_GOV_LADDER): which of the game's off-screen render targets are drawn at ACZ_VR_GOV_OFFRT_SCALE instead of PS2_UPSCALE while the lever is shed (at level 0 every target as before: the same images). `auto`: every slot that qualifies in the frame's draw list -- not the scene, the displayed target or the cockpit screens' target; no DATE draw into it, no colour clamp pass, AC5 native pass or cockpit / HUD copy; no depth buffer shared with another slot and its depth never sampled (the sun-occlusion probe reads one target's depth: left alone); no draw lays it about 1:1 (0.75-1.5 texels a pixel) onto the scene or the displayed target; its drawn part at least 1/32 of the target; 8 frames in a row. In the missions measured these are the glow / speed-blur chain (a half-size copy of the scene, its quarter and eighth reductions, laid back over the scene 2x magnified), the sun glow overlay (128 x 128 stretched over the screen), the sea's reflection (256 x 256, sampled in perspective by the sea), the game's cloud sprite textures and targets nothing samples. A list (`7,9,10`) takes only those slots (slot numbers follow the order a session first draws its targets: check `rt-census:` / `offrt:` lines; the 1:1 rule is then not applied, the others are); `0` = the lever has nothing to shed. Each shed slot keeps a second colour + depth pair at the lower scale (made one a frame, ~0.8-1.4 ms each at 4x, once the slot has qualified for 2 s while the governor runs: `offrt:` lines), swapped in at a frame start with its picture blitted across: a switch allocates nothing and keeps the content. Measured (exclusive 4x, user settings, in-run A/B): what the off-screen targets cost at all (PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=rtskip, governor off) M4 0.66-0.69 ms of 4.4 (game and in-between frames alike), M14 sea 0.28 +- 0.05, M12 overcast 0.18 +- 0.05; the lever M4 -0.17..-0.23 ms, M12 / M14 0 +- 0.04-0.07 (there the cost is the 128 x 128 object / cloud sprite textures, laid onto the scene near 1:1 by near sprites, and the sun-occlusion probe chain: left alone). Same frame (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=offrt, M4): > 8 levels on 0.001-0.08 % of the pixels, at most 24 levels, only at the edges of the speed-blur overlay over the ground (noise floor 0 % / 5 levels); M12 / M14 at their noise floor. A switch costs one frame +0.3-0.4 ms of GPU (all slots' copies in two barrier calls, only of slots something samples, one layer for one-view targets; no late frame in the traces); the lower versions are made with the full ones in the mission's loading frames (~0.9 ms and ~15 MB each at 4x) | @@ACZ_VR_GOV_OFFRT@@ |

What it does (bug #89, fx_pacing 2026-10-23): every headset frame shows the world at its display time minus one steady latency -- game frames too, not only the in-between frames. A game frame that reaches the headset a refresh late (its list published just after the renderer's decision, a runtime skip) or between refreshes (90 Hz: three refreshes per two game frames) is extrapolated / interpolated (alpha -0.6..1.5 of a game frame) by the same reprojection as the in-between frames; game time = the field clock's grid at the frame's first publication (the earliest publication of the last 128 fields anchors it); the latency = display time - game time of each game frame's first display, averaged over 32 game frames (resynced after a jump of 50 ms). Game frames within 0.02 of their slot stay exactly as drawn (a steady 120 Hz headset: identical images); they keep the game frame's work (cloud optics etc.). Game frames of two fields (the game below 60 fps) are extrapolated over their real length. Simulator, layered (M3, in-run A/B, tools/perf/cadence_ab.py): 90 Hz motion rms (q - 1) 0.408 -> 0.008, steps off by > 35 % 66.4 % -> 0 %, in-between alpha 0.67 -> 0.50, game frames moved +-0.18, the shown world's age 23.8 -> 24.8 ms (spread 3.2 -> 1.0); emulated 72 Hz (PS2_XR_TEST_HZ) rms 0.366 -> 0.009, jerks 16.8 % -> 0 %, alpha 0.83 -> 0.51, game frames moved +-0.22, age +1.0 ms (spread 4.3 -> 0.5). HIGH = every row at its default (`def`), i.e. today's picture, by construction (a row whose default changes stays HIGH's). Rows (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH): RESOLUTION 2X / 3X / 4X, FOREST DISTANCE NORMAL / FAR / FAR, FRAME-TIME GOVERNOR ON / ON / OFF, COCKPIT ANTI-ALIASING 2X / 2X / 4X (only while no COCKPIT DETAIL row exists: that row carries the MSAA rule); CLOUD DETAIL / CANOPY QUALITY / COCKPIT DETAIL low / medium / high (found by their row keys `cloud_detail`, `canopy_quality`, `cockpit_detail`; ENH_HAVE_CLOUD_DETAIL / ENH_HAVE_CANOPY_QUALITY in ps2_settings.c compile in the rows for `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_DETAIL` / `ACZ_VR_CANOPY_QUALITY`). Sweep (sim, RTX 3090 Ti, exclusive, the user's settings, layered, governor off, PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2 halved; GPU ms per game / in-between frame): M3 J35J 4x 3.36 / 1.19, 3x 2.39 / 0.79, 2x 1.60 / 0.48; M1 overcast F-5E 3.76 / 2.87, 2.51 / 1.82, 1.72 / 1.14; M18 X-02S 2.91 / 1.86, 2.03 / 1.21, 1.27 / 0.68; the 120 Hz pair 3x -30..-35 %, 2x -54..-59 %; T(S) = a + b S^2 leaves 69-74 % of a game frame and 79-84 % of an in-between frame pixel-proportional at 4x. Cockpit at 2 samples (in-run A/B in the same runs): -0.01..-0.04 game, -0.01..-0.06 in-between in these light cockpits. FOREST DISTANCE is not measured today (no trees in view in these flights; 10-21: M2 +0.38 ms at FAR). No other GPU was measured and nothing ran in the headset. ### Quest Touch controllers

The Touch controllers as the pilot's controls (`runtime/src/ps2_touch.c`; the OpenXR actions in `runtime/src/ps2_xr.c`;
CONTROLS_RESEARCH_2026-10-23.md). Everything ends as DualShock 2 bytes: the game, PS2PAD2 recordings and replays are
unchanged; the Xbox pad stays live (per axis the larger input wins, buttons are OR'ed).

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACZ_TOUCH` | `auto` (ctl_priority 2026-11-03; was off) | `auto`, `pad`, `stick`, `off` / `0` | Quest Touch controllers as input (needs `PS2_XR=1`; off = no OpenXR action set at all). `auto` (unset; ENHANCEMENTS > CONTROLS > TOUCH CONTROLLERS = AUTO) = `pad` while no gamepad is connected (the controller registry, ACZ_PAD_ACTIVE), muted while one is (no input to the game, no vibration, the cockpit's hands as with off) unless Touch is the active controller: forced, or by a press on it, and a hand closing on the stick or throttle makes the session `stick` (ACZ_TOUCH_AUTO_GRAB); a PS2_XR_TEST_TOUCH script without ACZ_TOUCH stays `pad`. `pad` = Touch as an Xbox pad with the the modern layout positions through the controller layout (left thumbstick flies, triggers = triggers, grips = bumpers with an analog value above a resting hand (0.3), A B X Y as on the pad, right thumbstick flicks = D-pad, right click = R3 on release, left click = View (tap: map; held 1 s: recentre), both clicks = L3, Menu = Menu on release (held 0.5 s = View + Menu: the quit / ENHANCEMENTS combo)). `stick` = while flying the right hand grabs a virtual stick with the grip (tilt relative to the grab = pitch / roll) and the left hand the throttle lever (the left thumbstick also thrust while held: ACZ_TOUCH_THUMB_THRUST); trigger gun, A missile / special, B target, X weapon switch, Y map (held 1 s recentre), right thumbstick flicks = wingman commands, its click = view, left click = autopilot, Menu = Start (held 1 s in flight: the TOUCH CONTROLS card, ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_HOLD); outside flight (menus, pause, events) as `pad`. The TOUCH CONTROLS card draws both mappings (bug #239) | @@ACZ_TOUCH@@ |

The button that closed the hand holds it (ACZ_TOUCH_GRIP: hold or tap); while a trigger holds, that hand's grip is its gun / brake. It stays so for the session; a pad press mutes Touch again (the hands let go, the lever back at CRUISE), the next Touch press brings it back. `1`: the GRAB WITH rule as it stands (under `either` the grip from anywhere; a pad-style player's grips are yaw in the modern layout, so a firm squeeze would flip the session). `0`: AUTO never grabs (before). The press rule, also for the switch beside a pad: trigger or grip past 0.65, thumbstick past 0.60 (release 0.35 / 0.30), a button; held 50 ms; 0.5 s after the controller binds, a control already held at binding not until released; not while the active pad holds something past a quarter of its travel or did within 0.5 s, or a pad is forced. | `ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_DZ` | `1.0` | degrees `0`..`5` | STICK: inner dead zone of the tilt (the game's own 64-of-127 per-axis dead zone is always skipped: the output starts at its edge) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_DZ@@ |

| `ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_RELEASE` | `0.2` | seconds `0`..`2` | STICK: the stick eases back to centre over this time when let go (also 0.3 s after the orientation stops being tracked) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_RELEASE@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_FRAME` | `hand` | `hand`, `cockpit` | STICK: pitch / roll are measured about gravity-up axes turned to the hand's heading at the grab (a forearm angled inwards does not mix roll into pitch), or about the cockpit's own axes | @@ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_FRAME@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_TWIST` | `0` | `1` | STICK: twisting the wrist also yaws (as the left thumbstick X; the larger wins) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_STICK_TWIST@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_THROTTLE` | `lever` | `lever`, `spring`, `tilt`, `thumbstick` | STICK: the left hand's throttle. `lever` = grab and move the hand fore/aft (CRUISE -> MIL forward, CRUISE -> IDLE back, then the air brake; an AB gate past MIL; haptic detents); it stays where it is let go. `spring` = the same, back to CRUISE when let go (the PS2's semantics). `tilt` = the lever follows the left controller's fore/aft tilt (25 deg per range; immune to position-tracking loss). `thumbstick` = left thumbstick Y as the PS2's spring throttle (X still yaws: the dominant axis wins) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_THROTTLE@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_THROTTLE_CM` | `8` | cm `3`..`20` | STICK lever: hand travel from CRUISE to MIL and from CRUISE to IDLE (the air brake takes half a range more, the AB gate 1.5 cm past MIL) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_THROTTLE_CM@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_THUMB_THRUST` | on | `0` | (bug #239, touch_ux 2026-10-29: "how do I speed up") STICK with the lever, spring or tilt throttle: the left thumbstick's up / down is thrust / air brake while it is held, over the lever's setting (up: at least `0.9 x (deflection - 0.15) / 0.8 / 0.97` of the way to MIL, full up = the afterburner with the AB gate's haptic tick; down: at most `-(deflection - 0.15) / 0.8`, the air brake past 60 %); released: the lever's setting again; the yaw then takes the thumbstick's X only where X is the larger axis (as ACZ_TOUCH_THROTTLE=thumbstick). The cockpit's lever shows the result. `0` = the thumbstick's Y does nothing (as before) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_THUMB_THRUST@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_POSE_TIME` | `now` | `now`, `display` | Which controller pose the stick and lever read: the pose at the poll's own time (needs the runtime's host-time conversion, XR_KHR_win32_convert_performance_counter_time; else `display`), or the frame's predicted display time (27-39 ms ahead on Link: lower latency, but the extrapolation overshoots at stops and amplifies tremor). The drawn hands always use the display time | @@ACZ_TOUCH_POSE_TIME@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_RS` | `dpad` | `dpad`, `look` | Right thumbstick: D-pad flicks (wingman commands, menus) or the game's right stick | @@ACZ_TOUCH_RS@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_HAPTICS` | `0.5` | `0`..`1` | Controller vibration strength on Touch: the game's rumble (both motors), weather / debris / buffet rumble, and the STICK cues (scaled from their 0.5 design level) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_HAPTICS@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_CUES` | `detent,ab,gun,missile` | words `detent` `ab` `gun` `missile` `centre`, `all`, `0` | STICK haptic cues: throttle detents (12-15 ms ticks), the AB gate (20 ms + a faint 2 s fade), gun pulses (25 ms at 12 Hz on the stick hand while the round count drops), a missile thump (60 ms), the stick crossing its centre (5 ms) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_CUES@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_REACH` | `0` | metres | STICK: only grab when the hand is within this distance of the cockpit's stick / throttle grip point (`ps2_ctl.stick_grip`, needs a cockpit with animated controls); `0` = grab anywhere | @@ACZ_TOUCH_REACH@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_SWAP` | `0` | `1` | Left-handed: the controllers swap roles (stick in the left hand, throttle in the right) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_SWAP@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_AUTOPAUSE` | `0` | `1` | STICK: a Start tap (pause) when the headset loses focus while a grab is held in flight | @@ACZ_TOUCH_AUTOPAUSE@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_CARD` | `auto` | `auto`, `1`, `0` | (bug #239) The TOUCH CONTROLS card (`runtime/src/ps2_quit.c`: both Quest controllers drawn from above in the ENHANCEMENTS page's look, every control with a leader line to what it does now -- HANDS ON STICK or AS A PAD, left / right shows the other mode -- and four lines of essentials; on the same headset quad as the page) by itself: `auto` = once, the first time HANDS ON STICK is used with both controllers bound and the headset focused (1.5 s into a menu between missions, or 2.5 s into a flight, which it pauses with a Start press and resumes when the card closes; saved as `[input] touch_controls_seen = 1` when it closes; re-asked up to 5 times if a flight starts under it), `1` = at every start, `0` = never by itself. On demand: pause menu > TOUCH CONTROLS (ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_ROW), Menu held in flight (ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_HOLD), ENHANCEMENTS > CONTROLS > SHOW TOUCH CONTROLS (also F4). B, Y, A or Menu closes it; the game sees a neutral pad while it is up | @@ACZ_TOUCH_CARD@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_HOLD` | `1.0` | seconds `0`, `0.6`..`5` | (bug #239) STICK in flight: holding Touch's Menu button this long pauses the game and shows the TOUCH CONTROLS card (resumed when it closes); a tap is still Start; the View + Menu combo is no longer sent in flight (it only showed "pause first" there). `0` = off (the old Menu hold) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_HOLD@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_ROW` | on | `0` | (bug #239) With ACZ_TOUCH `pad` / `stick`: the in-mission pause menu gets a TOUCH CONTROLS row after ENHANCEMENTS (the game's row, font and cursor, as ENHANCEMENTS; campaign: 8 rows, QUIT GAME's YES / CANCEL at y 265 / 290, inside the panel); choosing it shows the card over the paused game. `0` = no row | @@ACZ_TOUCH_CARD_ROW@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_HINTS` | on | `0` | (bug #239: the user flew 23 s without squeezing the grip, "the stick does not move") STICK in flight: when the stick hand's controller turns more than 25 deg within a second while the stick is not held, a short panel says TAKE THE STICK -- "Squeeze and hold the RIGHT grip, then tilt the controller" (4 s; at most 3 times, 20 s apart, none once the stick has been taken twice). AUTO, bug #314: the one line PULL THE TRIGGER TO TAKE THE STICK (ACZ_TOUCH_AUTO_GRAB) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_HINTS@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_TITLE_START` | on | `0` | (the first public report of the Quest build, 2026-11-17: "stuck on the title screen, none of my controller inputs work") Touch as a pad on the game's PRESS START BUTTON screen: a press of A, X or either trigger is a Start tap too, beside the left controller's Menu button (Start everywhere); the control itself reaches the game again once it is let go, so the main menu never sees it held. Only that screen: not the logos, the menus or a movie. `0` = Menu alone, as before | @@ACZ_TOUCH_TITLE_START@@ |
| `ACZ_TOUCH_GAME_DZ` | `64` | counts `0`..`120` | The game's per-axis stick dead zone the virtual stick (and ACZ_PAD_STICK_REMAP) start at: byte = 128 +- (64 + 63 s) | @@ACZ_TOUCH_GAME_DZ@@ |
| `ACZ_PAD_STICK_REMAP` | `0` | `1` | Gamepad (and Touch PAD) left stick: its travel starts at the game's dead-zone edge instead of the centre (a 4-count inner dead zone), so the first part of the stick's travel is not dead | @@ACZ_PAD_STICK_REMAP@@ |
| `PS2_XR_TEST_TOUCH` | off | `"field:hand:key=value,... field~hand:key=value,..."` (hand `L` / `R`; keys `grip` `trig` (0..1), `sx` `sy` (-1..1), `pitch` `roll` `yaw` (deg: top back / right, nose right), `px` `py` `pz` (m), `a`/`x` `b`/`y` `click` `menu` `ttouch` `thtouch` `rot` `pos` `act` `focus` (0/1)) | [test] Synthetic Touch controllers by vblank field, deterministic like PS2_XR_TEST_HEAD_SCRIPT: from its first entry a hand is synthetic (active, tracked, focused); each entry sets the keys it names; `~` ramps from the previous entry of that hand. Works without `ACZ_TOUCH` (then pad mode) | @@PS2_XR_TEST_TOUCH@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_TOUCH` | off | fields | [debug] Every N fields: focus, per hand activity / tracking / grip / trigger / thumbstick, the stick's tilt and bytes, the lever, the PS2 bytes sent, the pose age, haptic calls, and the cockpit interface (`ps2_ctl`); plus grab / release / detent / haptic-cue events | @@ACZ_DEBUG_TOUCH@@ |

## VR HUD

How the game's 2D HUD is resized and placed in head-tracked frames (`runtime/src/ps2_video.c`, anchor maths in `runtime/src/ps2_xr.c`).

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_SCALE` | `1.0` (ENHANCEMENTS HUD SIZE: `1.3`) | multiplier; `0` = off | HUD size relative to its original angular size (1 = pitch ladder matches the horizon) | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_SCALE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_TAN_H` | `0.5625` | tangent | The game's own horizontal half-FOV tangent, the reference for HUD scaling | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_TAN_H@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_TAN_V` | `0.4219` | tangent | The game's own vertical half-FOV tangent | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_TAN_V@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_ANCHOR` | on | `0` | Keep the direction HUD (ladder, heading tape, aircraft symbol) on the aircraft's nose in world-locked frames | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_ANCHOR@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_ANCHOR_BOX` | `0.42,0.62,0.45` | `"x,up,down"` (half-screen units) or `all` | Middle zone whose HUD draws count as direction HUD and get anchored; `all` anchors everything | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_ANCHOR_BOX@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_RADIO_PLANE` | on in the PS2_RQ build (the Quest and the PC test build of the renderer; the PC build has no such code) | `0` | (rq4_views 2026-11-11, BUGS_RQ R-95; the user's M4 flight 49.5-52.3 s: "the HUD doubles in head turns") The radio texts (the subtitles: flat HUD draws at depth ~6e-8, the RCL_RADIO of ACZ_REC_CLEAN) all on the cockpit plane (ACZ_VR_HUD_COCKPIT_DIST), as one block. The block lies across the upper edge of the middle zone (ACZ_VR_HUD_ANCHOR_BOX), so the zone split it by each draw's centre: the third line (game y 82..110, with the heading tape) anchored at infinity, the lines above on the plane with SCORE and TIME; every millimetre the eyes left the reference point slid them apart by 1 / 0.55 m (device dumps of the user's tape: 1.7 px a mm of sideways travel, up to ~6 deg in the head shake): lines over lines in the turning frames, one block at rest. Chosen by the depth, not the place, so no line flips anchor as the game scrolls the text; the heading tape, the ladder and the rest of the zone keep their anchor. `0` = by the zone as before. `hud-radio:` (every 3600 radio-text draws): in the zone, at infinity, on the plane, and radio-depth draws a HUD block or marker took | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_RADIO_PLANE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_COCKPIT_DIST` | `0.55` | metres; `0` = in front of the eyes | Cockpit frames: the rest of the HUD (radar, boxes, weapons) sits on a plane this far ahead of the eye point | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_COCKPIT_DIST@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER` | on | `0` | Keep each target box's label (TGT, FRND...) with its box: no HUD scaling or anchoring, at infinity like the box, same reprojection (before: the label was moved 15-20 deg away) | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_SCALE` | `1` | factor | Scale target boxes, their depth-tested copies and their labels together about the box centre | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_SCALE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE` | `1` | `0` | (bug #316, 2026-11-05: "from afar it is a mess of all these squares ... a bit smaller, not tiny, so they do not cover the target") A target box's size is a curve of the target's range, on top of ACZ_VR_MARKER_SCALE: the box, its depth-tested copy, a far target's bracket frame and the red lock diamond; the text beside the box keeps its size and follows the box's edge. The range is the box's own: its depth-tested copy lies at the target's depth (calibrated against the units' places, see NOTES). `0` = the game's size, these draws byte for byte. The curve is our design: no published source says how the newer games size theirs. ACZ_DEBUG_MARKER=1 logs range and scale now and then | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_NEAR` | `1000` | metres | (bug #316) Up to this range a box has its full size | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_NEAR@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_FAR` | `8000` | metres | (bug #316) From this range on a box has ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_FAR_SCALE; straight in log range between NEAR and FAR (the same factor per doubling) | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_FAR@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_FAR_SCALE` | `0.5` | factor `0.35`..`1` | (bug #316) The size at FAR and beyond; below 0.35 it is held at 0.35, the legible floor (~1.7 deg in the headset at TARGET BOX SIZE 1X) | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_FAR_SCALE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_AB` | off | `1` | [test] (bug #316) Odd game frames at the game's size, even ones by range: PS2_XR_DUMP_PAIR=2 dumps the two sizes of one target one game frame apart in one run | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_RANGE_AB@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_INFO` | on | `0` | (bug #135, 2026-10-27, M5: "again this box with the distance moves away from the aircraft") Everything the game writes beside a target box stays with the box: the selected target's name and distance (two HUD-green lines right of the box, above its top and below its bottom), a friendly's callsign / order lines in its blue (also right-aligned to the box's left edge; long callsigns were cut at 48 px) and the red diamond the game puts on a locked target's box (depth test ALWAYS at the target's depth, so taken for HUD) -- drawn where the game put them, at infinity like the box, scaled with ACZ_VR_MARKER_SCALE, hidden by the frames like it, instead of being scaled and anchored like the HUD (x 0.53 across / 0.40 up-down at HUD SIZE 1.3, towards the gun cross: M10 at 295 m with the box 21 deg above the view centre, the name / distance and the red lock diamond sat 16-17 deg below it). Info glyphs: at most 12 px, the box's texture, any colour, 48 px left .. 80 px right and 16 px above / below the box, straight after it in the draw order; a marker sprite: from the boxes' texture, 6-40 px, a depth between the radio texts' (~6e-8) and the HUD's (1). `0` = as before | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_INFO@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_FRAME` | on | `0` | (cv2_vis 2026-10-27, M7 13:50:40: "this square that moves should stay in the collimator, but it is not only in the collimator") The bracket frame the game draws around a far selected target's box (M7's CTRL TOWER at 60-100 km: ~48 x 45 PS2 px of plain lines with corner ticks, in the box's own colour and faint alpha, 75,255,55,22) stays with the box: drawn where the game put it, at infinity, scaled with ACZ_VR_MARKER_SCALE about the box's centre, hidden by the cockpit like the box. Before, it classified as HUD (untextured depth-ALWAYS lines in the HUD's middle zone), was scaled about the boresight (x 0.53 / 0.38 at HUD SIZE 1.3) and anchored to the aircraft, so it sat at about half the target's angle from the nose (7-13 deg below the nose in a 25 deg climb for a target 25 deg below), apart from the box, the name and the distance it frames on the PS2. Matched: untextured HUD-class lines in a box's exact colour and alpha within 32 PS2 px of a box of this or the last frame. `0` = as before | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_FRAME@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_ROLL` | on | `0` | (hud_world 2026-10-28, bug #151, M7 22:55:26 "this ACC should not turn like that", M8 23:37:28 "the icons turn here too") Target boxes, their labels (TGT, FRND), names and distances, the red lock diamond, a far target's bracket frame and the bombs' / rockets' aiming ellipse lean with the aircraft, as on the PS2, whose screen is fixed to the aircraft: each is turned about its box's centre by the aircraft's roll as seen at that place (the angle between the head camera's up and the aircraft's up / right direction there, the same perspective as the anchored HUD). The game renders with the head's camera, roll included, and draws them upright on its image: with the head rolled 25 deg against the cockpit they stood 25 deg off the cockpit and the rest of the HUD, and turned against it with every head roll. Place, size and shape stay the game's; head-locked frames untouched. Sim: head roll 25 -> boxes and text turned 25.0 deg (ACZ_DEBUG_MARKER logs it). `0` = upright to the eye, as before | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_ROLL@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_BLINK` | on | `0` | (hud_world 2026-10-28, bug #151, M7 22:51:18-24: CTRL TOWER's name, distance and frame small and off to one side every other tenth of a second) The game blinks some target boxes (a ground target under the RCL's ellipse: 10 fields drawn, 10 not) but writes their name / distance (and a far selected target's bracket frame) every field; without the box they followed the box drawn before them, the distance line (13-22 px below) and the frame went the HUD's way: x 0.53 / 0.40 towards the boresight and anchored. Now a HUD-green info glyph that continues the boxes' chain but not where the game writes a box's text (name 3 px right of the box, 9 px above its top; distance under its bottom) and starts a new line stands in for the missing 16 x 13 box (3 px left of it, 9 px below its top), which takes its text and frame like a drawn box. Sim (M7, RCL near CTRL TOWER, head swept +-12 deg and rolled 20): glyphs near a box sent to the HUD path 6,996 in 453 fields -> 0. `0` = as before | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_BLINK@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM` | on | `0` | (hud_world 2026-10-28, bug #152, M7 A-10A 23:20:58 "it must show exactly where the bomb hits") The bombs' and rocket pods' aiming ellipse (HUD atlas cell s 2..39, t 125..162, 36 x 31 PS2 px) is placed by the game where its camera -- the head-turned one in VR -- sees the impact point (rockets: the boresight); the bombs' fall line (5 dashes, untextured lines with the FST bit, right after the ellipse) runs from the game's screen centre to the ellipse's edge. Both were HUD-scaled about the boresight and anchored: the ellipse 5.6 deg off the impact direction with the head straight, 14.2 / 17.2 deg with the head turned (yaw 20 pitch -10 / yaw -15 pitch -25 roll 15; M7 FAEB dive). Now the ellipse stays at the game's place (at infinity, turning with the world between game frames), at the HUD's size (HUD SIZE about its own centre) and with the aircraft's lean (ACZ_VR_MARKER_ROLL), hidden by the cockpit like a box: 0.00 / 0.26 / 0.08 deg off; the fall line runs from the aircraft's boresight (the HUD's gun cross) to that ellipse's edge, its dashes spread over the new length. `0` = both drawn as HUD, as before | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM_LINE` | on | `0` | (hud_place 2026-10-31, bug #256, M13 F-117A 11:45:02 "with the head's movement the bomb's trajectory line moves; it should not be so", 11:46:28 "something peeks through ahead, some sprite") The guided bombs' (GPB) fall line: 5-12 untextured dashes without the FST bit (the UGB / FAEB line's 5 have it), drawn right after the aiming ellipse in its colour, from the round symbol at the game's screen centre (the head's forward in VR; it slides in from the screen's edge when the line appears) to the ellipse's edge. They took the HUD's way: scaled about the boresight, those in the HUD's middle zone anchored to the aircraft, the rest on the cockpit plane 0.55 m ahead (M13, head yaw 12 pitch -6: 4 of 12 dashes at 0.55 m, the line in pieces outside the combiner and over the HUD body, sliding with every head turn). Now they are recognised as the fall line (the run of lines right after the ellipse, in its colour, on one straight line through its centre) and drawn as ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM draws it: from where the HUD shows that round symbol (at rest the gun cross) to the ellipse, which stays 40-43 game px under the boresight at every head pose -- the line now holds still with the head at yaw 12 / pitch -6, yaw -10 / pitch 4, yaw 15, pitch 10 and roll 25 (ev/gpb_*); it never runs past the gun cross or into the ellipse. `0` = the GPB dashes on the HUD path as before (the FST dashes keep ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM) | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_AIM_LINE@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_MARKER` | off | `1`, `2` | [debug] Log the box/label associations (with each box's texels, filter and blend; the first info glyph of each box, the HUD-class box copies kept with their box) and, every 3000 draws, how many symbols at infinity come before the cockpit model / the edge AA pass; `2` also every HUD draw from a box's texture within 96 px of it that stays HUD (`not label`) | @@ACZ_DEBUG_MARKER@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_SHARP` | `3` | `0`, `1`, `2` | How target boxes draw their texels (labels and the rest of the HUD keep the smooth replacement): `3` = the texels as the line drawing they are (gs.frag marker_lines, bug #98: the ground targets' octagons and cube icons were "too pixelated" in `2` -- their diagonal outlines are single texels touching at the corners, drawn as staircases of beads): every lit texel a node, 8-adjacent nodes joined by straight segments (a diagonal chain a straight line 0.8 texel wide, a dot a disc, a dash a capsule), the game's anti-aliasing fringe (a texel next to one over 3.3x as bright) left out, no filled corners, one-pixel anti-aliased edge; square boxes look as in `2`; `2` = each original texel as a crisp shape at the exact sub-pixel place the sprite maps it to -- a one-pixel anti-aliased edge, lit neighbours joined, outer corners rounded (a lone dot a disc, a dash a capsule), every texel row kept (the game squashes the 16 x 16 cell into 16 x 13 pixels and its point filter drops rows) and smooth motion instead of whole-game-pixel steps (bug #67: `1` looked pixelated in the headset at ~8 display pixels per texel); needs the boxes' own blend by the source alpha, else `1`; `1` = flat, one colour per original texel on the game's pixel grid (bug #48, 2026-10-22); `0` = the 4x Real-ESRGAN atlas (blurred beads) | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_SHARP@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_ROUND` | on | `0` | With ACZ_VR_MARKER_SHARP=2: the cells' outer corners rounded (half a texel); `0` = square cells with anti-aliased edges | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_ROUND@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_MARKER_AB` | off | frames N | [test] The target boxes as line drawings (ACZ_VR_MARKER_SHARP=3) and as shapes (`2`) in alternate blocks of N frames; the mean GPU time per frame of each logged every 40 blocks (`marker-ab:`); `PS2_PERF_AB=1 PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=markerlines` gives the exact same-frame image A/B | @@ACZ_VR_MARKER_AB@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_OCCLUDE` | on | `0` | Frames with the 3D cockpit model: target boxes, their labels and the collimated middle of the HUD (gun cross, and ladder / heading tape where shown) are drawn only where no part of the model is in front -- seen through the canopy and the HUD glass, cut by frames, the HUD body and the glare shield (depth bounds, like the sun); `0` draws them over the model as before | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_OCCLUDE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_HUD_GHOST` | `0` | `0`..`1` | Opacity of a faint copy of hidden target boxes and labels drawn over the cockpit model (try 0.25-0.35); `0` = hidden completely | @@ACZ_VR_HUD_GHOST@@ |

Defaults: Half-Life: Alyx's spectator camera (vr_camera_decay_yaw_pitch_halflife 0.09, roll 0.5), position ~0.1 s as other VR spectator cameras. The aircraft's own motion is never lagged (the camera rides the game frame's aircraft camera). Sim, 1.5 deg head jitter (PS2_XR_TEST_HEAD_JITTER): M1 4x, frame-to-frame steps (RMS) head -> camera: yaw 0.231 -> 0.063 deg, pitch 0.249 -> 0.067, roll 0.130 -> 0.007, position 1.07 -> 0.32 mm; a scripted 60 deg turn reaches 90 % 67 ms after the head; during turns the camera is 3.2 deg (max 10.7) off the head, pulled in on 39 of 400 frames (a private script) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_SMOOTH@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_ROLL` | `smooth` | `smooth`, `lock` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the head's roll smoothed (its half-life, ACZ_REC_CINE_SMOOTH) or `lock`ed: no head roll at all, the view level with the cockpit (the aircraft's bank stays) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_ROLL@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_PITCH` | `0` | degrees, `-20`-`20` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the view tilted up (+) or down (-) from the smoothed head, about its own x axis: more sky and less instrument panel for flat-screen framing (0: where the pilot looks) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_PITCH@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_MARGIN` | `1` | degrees | ACZ_REC_CINE: how far inside the frame's field of view (what the game drew for the head) the view's corners and edges must stay; the smoothed camera is pulled towards the head as far as needed (a fast head turn is followed at about the margin's distance: 85 deg across leaves ~10.5 deg sideways, ~26 deg up / down) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_MARGIN@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_WINDOW` | `2560x1440` (with ACZ_REC_CINE) | `WxH`, `full`, `keep` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the game window's size in pixels while the view is on -- the OBS canvas of "ACZ VR cine" (obs_setup.py ACZ_REC_CINE_RES); not saved to ac5_settings.ini. `full` = borderless on the window's monitor at its desktop size (3840x2160 here: the screen is covered), `keep` = the configured window. Logged with the desktop's mode and scale (`rec-cine: window`) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_WINDOW@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_FILTER` | `bicubic` | `bicubic`, `bilinear` | ACZ_REC_CINE: how the window resamples the view's rectangle (present.frag mode 3: Catmull-Rom in nine bilinear taps, crisper edges than bilinear when upscaling 1364 x 664 to 2560 x 1440; a view drawn at more pixels than the window, ACZ_REC_CINE_SCALE, is sampled down instead: up to 4 x 4 bilinear taps averaged) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_FILTER@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_SCALE` | `1` (the eyes' density; a recording's height) | `1`; a multiple below 100 (`1.5`, `2`, ...); `1080`, `1440`, `2160` or `4k` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the view's own pixel density (bug #245, rec_cine2 2026-10-30). `1`: drawn at the eyes' upscale (PS2_UPSCALE), so at 4x / 85 deg the view's rectangle has 1364 x 664 pixels, resampled up to the window (as before). A height: the upscale S whose 16:9 rectangle holds about that many pixels, chosen at the first camera (4x / 85 deg: 1080 -> 6x, 2045 x 997; 1440 -> 8x, 2727 x 1329; 2160 -> 12x, 4090 x 1993; a narrower ACZ_REC_CINE_FOV takes a larger S for the same pixels); a multiple: S = it x PS2_UPSCALE; at most 16 and the device's image size; no more than the eyes' = the eyes'. The pass then records at S (rt_scale = S while it runs; every other target keeps its own scale): private targets at S for the scene, the displayed target, the depth their draws use and any slot laid about 1:1 onto them (cine_plan `big`; Zero's glow / blur chain stays at the frame's scale), the cockpit's 4x MSAA target and the canopy's world window-sized (a viewport moved by the window clip's corner; cockpit_comp.frag push `org`), the effects' depth snapshot the view's own, our near clouds from the frame's buffer through the two densities' homography; the window samples the rectangle down (present.frag downsample). Same frame at both densities (ACZ_REC_CINE_DUMP_PAIR; a private script): instrument lettering, dials, the canopy frame's edges and the canopy drops resolve (mean |Laplacian| of the window x1.4-1.6, of the instrument panel x1.8-2.6), the 2006 terrain and cloud textures change little. Cost (sim, exclusive 4x, governor off, ACZ_REC_CINE_AB, M1 F-5E in the cockpit, per game frame that draws the view): `1` (1364 x 664, 0.9 Mpx) +0.94 ms; `1080` (6x, 2045 x 997, 2.0 Mpx) +1.42 (median +1.46); `1440` (8x, 2727 x 1329, 3.6 Mpx) +2.10 (+2.23); `2.25` (9x, 3068 x 1495: 1440 in both axes, 4.6 Mpx) +2.50 (+2.64); `2160` (12x, 4090 x 1993, 8.2 Mpx) +3.93 -- about 0.55 ms + 0.41 ms per million pixels of the view (the frame itself 3.45-3.51 ms; two earlier runs with the GPU shared, frame 5.0-5.3 ms, gave +3.06 / +3.30 for 1080 / 1440); a narrower FOV does not make a native height cheaper (the same pixels); renderer CPU 0.49 -> 0.57-0.65 ms a view. VRAM of the view (images made at its first frames): 448 MB at 1, 863 MB at 1080, 1.28 GB at 1440, 2.5 GB at 2160. Headset (x1.75, the in-between frame at 120 Hz, ~5.5 ms of its own): +1.65 ms at `1` (~7.2 ms: fits 8.33), +2.5 at 1080 (~8.0: no margin), +3.7-3.9 at 1440 (~9.3: over), +6.9 at 2160. At 90 Hz (the Meta Quest Link app's refresh rate; ps2_xr.c does not choose one) smooth motion draws one frame between game frames for every second game frame, so the view goes into the game frames (ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN): ~5.5-5.7 ms own of 11.1 -> 1080 ~8.1, 1440 ~9.3-9.6 (margin ~1.5 ms), 9x ~10.1, 2160 ~12.5 (72 Hz, 13.9 ms). Hence the default stays `1`; `record cine 1440` with the Link app at 90 Hz for a native 1440p master. The headset's image is unchanged (the pass after the eye copies; ACZ_REC_CINE_VERIFY at 1440: 40 passes, 0 changed); off and `1`: the same as before | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_SCALE@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN` | `between` | `between`, `game` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the view of a game frame is drawn in the frame drawn between it and the next game frame while smooth motion draws those (the headset's game frames, the heavier ones, keep their time; the window shows it from then on), else in the game frame itself; `game` = always in the game frame. `play_zero_desktop.sh record cine` sets `game` with the frame-exact recording (ACZ_REC_EXACT, bug #264): with `between` a game frame not followed by an in-between frame never had its view drawn (the 10-31 smooth sessions: 0-145 of 300 game frames per 5 s had none on the headset) and repeated the previous one in the recording | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_MONO` | on | `0` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the view is drawn in layer 0 only: in its pass the game's draws, meshes and the 3D cockpit put view 1's primitives off screen (gs.vert / mesh.vert push bit 262144, cockpit.vert misc.w 2): no fragments for the second, unused layer; `0` = both views as the eyes (the same image twice). With ACZ_REC_CINE_CULL: +0.89 instead of +1.44 ms a view (sim 4x M1) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_MONO@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_CULL` | on | `0` | ACZ_REC_CINE: the scene's world and sun draws wholly outside the view's box seen from the frame's camera (+8 PS2 px) are left out of its pass (native meshes by their screen box, GS draws of up to 4096 vertices by their vertices). M1: 39-48 % of the draws left out (85 / 70 deg) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_CULL@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_NEAR` | on | `0` | ACZ_REC_CINE: our near clouds (ACZ_VR_CLOUDS with the near field) in the view: the frame's near buffer (marched for the head) composited through a homography of the head's turn against the view's (cloud_comp.frag near_px; the eye's few cm left out). `0` = only the far clouds in the view | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_NEAR@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_AB` | off | N frames | [test] ACZ_REC_CINE: blocks of N frames of the kind that draws the view (ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN) with and without it (the "off" blocks show the frame's own image in the window); `rec-cine-ab:` the mean GPU ms of each every 40 N frames (a block's first 4 not counted) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_AB@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER` | on | `0` | (perf_judder 2026-10-31, bug #255) ACZ_REC_CINE: a frame that draws the view gives the headset its images first -- the part of the frame recorded so far (the scene, our passes, the eye copies, the headset depth, the quit prompt's layer) goes to the GPU, the eye images are released and the XR frame ended, and only then is the view recorded; the view, the window and the rest follow as the frame's next part (one more early submission). The same commands in the same order on one queue, a barrier over all commands between the parts: the same images in the headset and in the window. Before, the headset's frame waited for the view's recording on the renderer and for its GPU work, and its last part for the window's swapchain image. Sim 4x, Rafale M12, in-run A/B (ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER_AB=30, 18 pairs of 5-s windows): the headset's images ready 6.68 -> 4.97 ms after the recording start (-1.71 +- 0.04), the frame's own end 6.68 -> 7.04 (xrEndFrame between the parts; GPU idle, not GPU work). The view itself costs +1.55 (F-35C M14) to +1.72 ms (MiG-31 M11) of GPU a frame that draws it (ACZ_REC_CINE_AB; ~1.75x on the headset). Not in eye-dump frames that draw the frame again after the view (PS2_PERF_AB, PS2_XR_DUMP_NOCLOUD) nor with held parts (PS2_PERF_EARLY_DEFER). `0` = as before | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER_AB` | off | N frames | [test] ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER on and off in blocks of N frames that draw the view; the 5-s line `gpu-speed: frames that draw the cinematic view with / without ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER` gives each arm's latency to the headset's images (recording start after xrWaitFrame -> the GPU end of their part), how many were over the headset's period, and the frame's own end (tools/perf/judder_report.py prints the means) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_AFTER_AB@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT` | off (`play_zero_desktop.sh record cine`: `1`; `record cine noexact`: `0`) | `1` | The frame-exact recording (bug #264, rec_pace 2026-11-02): the runtime encodes the window itself instead of OBS sampling it. OBS's game capture copied the window at its presents (at most one per 16.67 ms of its own clock, `limit_framerate`) and its video thread took the newest copy at its own 60 Hz ticks; the window presents in the XR frame that picks a game frame up, on the headset's vsync, which drifts against the field clock: in phases the pickups alternate 1 / 3 refreshes at 120 Hz (8 / 25 ms) and the recordings repeated (and lost) about one game frame per 1-refresh step -- 8-20 a second (M18 11-01, nosmooth: repeats per 5 s = 0.86 x the 1-refresh steps + 7.3, r = 0.81 over 68 moving 5-s windows: 1.3 a second without such steps, 3.5 with, up to 13; OBS itself lagged 3 of 23 250 frames); in smooth mode the views of game frames without a following in-between frame were never drawn (ACZ_REC_CINE_WHEN=between; 10-31 smooth session: repeats per 5 s = 0.36 x the game frames without an in-between frame + 23.5, r = 0.57; 6.0 a second in all). Now, in the frame that shows a game frame's content in the window for the first time (the frame that drew the cinematic view, or a game frame showing its own image: menus, movies), the presented window (with the F4 overlay) is blitted into an RGBA8 image of the recording's size and converted to NV12 BT.709 limited (rx_nv12.comp) into a host buffer (ACZ_REC_EXACT_BUFFERS), tagged with the list's field on the real-time field count (the guest's count + the fields the clock dropped); a writer thread (ps2_recexact.c) sends each once, in field order, to ffmpeg (ACZ_REC_EXACT_FFMPEG) through a named pipe as raw NV12 at the field rate -- a field without an image of its own (the renderer skipped the list, a lost capture) repeats the previous image, counted -- and the game's own mix (the audio callback's chunks, from the video's first frame on the monotonic clock; 1 sample in 200 repeated or left out while more than 10 ms off the clock, silence when no audio comes) through a second pipe; ffmpeg writes ACZ_REC_EXACT_OUT (x264 as OBS's cine master, the game as track "Game"), pinned to the efficiency cores. The file plays in real time whatever the headset or the desktop does; the headset's images and timing are untouched (the capture is in the window's part of the frame, after the headset's). Log: `rec-exact:` lines (frames written, fields repeated, captures lost, renderer waits, audio corrections; every 30 s and at the end; GPU per capture every 1800 captures). Sim (4x, M1 F-5E, 2560x1440 window, exclusive, governor off): GPU per capture 0.62-0.67 ms (blit 0.025, NV12 0.028, the 5.3 MB copy to host memory 0.56-0.62: bus-bound, in the window's part after the headset's images, so the headset's image of that frame is not later; it can push the next frame's GPU start); 0 renderer waits and 0 lost captures over 75 s with a stand-in for OBS's light encode on the same E-cores; the writer's pipe write 1.4-1.7 ms a frame; the game track is the mix sample for sample (against PS2_AUDIO_WAV: one constant lag, 0.00 ms spread over 44 s; 0 clock corrections); in play no field repeated by the recorder (the remaining repeats are the game's own: a 126 ms hitch, the R3 switch, the crash replay). VRAM +20 MB (RGBA8 image + the NV12 buffer), host memory +127 MB. Windows only (ffmpeg.exe over named pipes): elsewhere `1` logs that the recording is off | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_OUT` | `out/rec_exact_<date>_<time>.mkv` (`record cine`: `~/Videos/ACZ_playtest/acz_cine_<date>_<time>.mkv`) | file path (`/` or `\`) | ACZ_REC_EXACT: the recording; ffmpeg's messages go to `<file>.ffmpeg.log` | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_OUT@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_FFMPEG` | `ffmpeg.exe` (on PATH) | file path | ACZ_REC_EXACT: the encoder (needs libx264, or hevc_nvenc for ACZ_REC_EXACT_ENCODER=nvenc) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_FFMPEG@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_ENCODER` | `x264` | `x264`, `nvenc` | ACZ_REC_EXACT: x264 on the CPU (as OBS's cine profile; bug #104) or NVENC HEVC constant QP, which Quest Link shares (~20 lost Link frames a second when OBS recorded with it) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_ENCODER@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_CRF` | `16` (nvenc: `17` = its QP) | number | ACZ_REC_EXACT: x264 CRF (near-lossless master, as ACZ_REC_CINE_CRF) or the NVENC QP | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_CRF@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_PRESET` | `superfast` (nvenc: `p4`) | x264 / NVENC preset | ACZ_REC_EXACT: the encoder's preset. superfast CRF 16 at 2560x1440 60 fps needs ~70 % of the 8 E-cores (87 fps capacity there, ACZ_REC_CINE_PRESET's measurement); OBS's light reference profile (ACZ_REC_CINE_REF_RES) is ~1/6 of that | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_PRESET@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_ARGS` | none | ffmpeg output options | [expert] ACZ_REC_EXACT: more options for ffmpeg's output (after the codec options, before the file name) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_ARGS@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_AFFINITY` | `auto` (the efficiency cores: logical processors 16-23 here) | `auto`, hex mask, `0` (Windows places it) | ACZ_REC_EXACT: the encoder process's processor affinity (as ACZ_REC_OBS_AFFINITY for OBS: the P-cores stay the game's) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_AFFINITY@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_BUFFERS` | `24` | `4`-`96` | ACZ_REC_EXACT: host buffers for the window captures (w x h x 1.5 bytes each: 5.3 MB at 2560x1440, 127 MB for 24), host-cached memory; they hold the frames while the encoder is behind (24 = 0.4 s, plus the pipe and the encoder's own queues) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_BUFFERS@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_WAIT` | `50` | ms | ACZ_REC_EXACT: with every buffer waiting for the encoder, the renderer waits this long for one (the video before the headset, the user's priority 2026-11-02) before it lets that capture go (the field repeats the previous image; counted as lost) | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_WAIT@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_EXACT_FRAMES` | off | N | [test] ACZ_REC_EXACT: the file ends (both inputs closed, the encoder waited for) after N frames while the game goes on: a complete file from a test run that is killed at its end | @@ACZ_REC_EXACT_FRAMES@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_TRACK` | off | file | [test] ACZ_REC_CINE: per game frame a CSV line -- field, seq, the head's and the camera's yaw / pitch / roll (deg), their angle apart, pulled in, the head's and the camera's position (mm), head-driven -- for plots of the smoothing (a private script) and as the session's recorded head track | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_TRACK@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_DUMP` | on | `0` | [test] ACZ_REC_CINE: the eye dumps (PS2_XR_DUMP_EYES) of a frame that draws the view also write the view's rectangle at the window's size (`eye_<field>_C.ppm`, bilinear blit) and the presented window itself (`eye_<field>_W.ppm`: what OBS records) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_DUMP@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_DUMP_PAIR` | off | `1` | [test] ACZ_REC_CINE_SCALE: an eye-dumped frame's view (drawn at the view's own upscale) is drawn a second time at the eyes' density from the same camera (the same game frame, the smoothing standing still), and both rectangles are written as drawn, without resampling (`eye_<field>_P<upscale>.ppm`, e.g. `_P8` and `_P4`): the same-frame quality comparison (a private script); the window keeps the first | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_DUMP_PAIR@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CINE_DEBUG` | off | N | [debug] ACZ_REC_CINE: a line every N views (`rec-cine: N views`): the recording time on the renderer, the slots drawn privately, the head's angle off the camera (now, mean, max), how often it was pulled in, the share of draws left out (ACZ_REC_CINE_CULL) | @@ACZ_REC_CINE_DEBUG@@ |
| `ACZ_REC_CLEAN_VERIFY` | off | N | [test] ACZ_REC_CLEAN: every N-th tail hashes the frame's host data the GPU reads (vertices, mesh records, indices, blocks, staged uploads) before and after it and logs a change (write-combined memory: tens of ms a hash, hence every N-th); eye dumps also write `eye_<field>_R_Rpost.ppm` (the headset's right image read again after the tail) | @@ACZ_REC_CLEAN_VERIFY@@ |

## VR cockpit model

The 3D stereo cockpit that replaces the game's own in the R3 view (`runtime/src/ps2_video.c`, model built by `tools/cockpit/`). The game lighting and shadows come from the native renderer's light blocks, so they need `PS2_RN_VP=1`.

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL` | unset (game cockpit) | path to a `.cpit` | Replace the game's R3 cockpit with this model, drawn in true stereo with live instruments | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MODEL@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_BRIGHT` | `1` with the game light, `0.85` with the fixed light | float | Brightness of the model | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_BRIGHT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AMBIENT` | `0.55` | float | Ambient light on the model | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AMBIENT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_GAME_LIGHT` | `1` | `0`/`1` | Light the model with the game's sun and sky lights; `0` uses a fixed light | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_GAME_LIGHT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SPEC` | `0.3` | float | Scale of the materials' specular shine (glass: its own sharp lobe, ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_GLASS_SHINE) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SPEC@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SHADOWS` | on | `0` | Sun shadow map (2048x2048) over the front cockpit | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SHADOWS@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SHADOW_SIZE` | `2048` (`1024` in the Quest build: `android_main`'s defaults) | a power of two `256`..`4096` | (Quest device session 2026-11-08, the user's option 2; Q-122) The sun shadow map's texels a side. cockpit.frag's filters take their texel from textureSize and the pass's depth bias is slope-scaled: a smaller map only softens the edges. Quest 3, M1 F-5E with LOD 1, governor off: 2048 17.05 ms a stereo frame, 1024 16.61, 512 16.62 (the shadows' remaining ~1.2 ms are the casters' second geometry pass and the 8-tap sampling, not the map's size); no visible change at 1x | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SHADOW_SIZE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_KEY_LIGHT` | `sun` | `sun`, `game` | Which of the game's three model lights is the cockpit's key light (its sun shadow map, highlights, the cloud volume's exit glare): `sun` = the light nearest C1's sun (S1) among those with at least a quarter of the brightest one's colour, within 35 deg, sticky (the last key stays unless another is clearly nearer); without one (night, no C1) the strongest, sticky (10 %). `game` = the strongest every frame (as before 2026-10-23: in M2 the fixed camera light (0, .707, .707) and the sun have equal colours and the pick flipped ~every 2.4 s -- 31 times in 35 s of straight flight -- so the cockpit's shadows and highlights jumped between two directions 60 deg apart and its lower half changed brightness by up to 14 %; in M3 the fixed light (colour 1.18) beats the sun (1.14), so the shadows came from above-behind whatever the sun did; M1, M4 (F-5E), M11: the sun is the strongest anyway) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_KEY_LIGHT@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_COCKPIT_KEY` | off | N | [debug] Log the game's three lights (cockpit frame, colour, angle to C1's sun) and the key light chosen every N frames, with the changes of the key and of the strongest light (`cockpit key:`) | @@ACZ_DEBUG_COCKPIT_KEY@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT` | `1` | `0`..`1` (strength; ENHANCEMENTS > COCKPIT > LIGHT FROM THE WORLD: ON `1` / SUBTLE `0.5` / OFF `0`) | The 3D cockpit lit by the world the eye images show (ov_light 2026-10-25; ps2_video.c `sl_*`, cockpit.frag): just before the cockpit is drawn, 15 8x8 patches of the left eye's world image are read back, each with its world elevation, and averaged over `_S` into three bands -- the sky above (> 20 deg), the horizon (-15..20), the ground (< -15; a band's brightest patch left out: the sun, a flare) -- that keep their last value while the head looks elsewhere (the light does not follow the gaze). The model is then lit by a sky dome over the world's up -- an upward face takes (2 sky + horizon) / 3, a vertical one (sky + 2 horizon + ground) / 4, a downward one (2 ground + horizon) / 3, means in linear light, plus the sun's bounce inside the cockpit (`_BOUNCE`), occluded by ao^(1/2.2) (the bake's share of the sky, in linear light) -- instead of the game's ambient and its non-key model lights (a light from straight above in M7, below in M1 / M4 / M11, a fixed camera light in M2-M4: made for the aircraft seen from outside); the key light (the sun: its shadows and highlights, the cloud shadow, the in-cloud light, the flashes) stays as before, highlights from the key light only. Fades in over the first ~1 s of world seen; at night (M11) off (`_NIGHT`); bands forgotten after 2 s without a cockpit drawn. Tornado, same-frame A/B (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=scenelight,glassspec, light runs, governor 0, 7 head poses), the cockpit's mean linear luminance after / before: M7 storm x0.61-0.65 (the wing plate's brightest parts 84/113/131 -> 64/80/91, the sky 60/75/85), M12 x0.73, M6 x0.86, M4 x1.02, M3 x1.07, M5 x1.31 (M11 at night: the game's lights, `_NIGHT`), M1 overcast over snow x1.76; the F-1 in M4 x0.50. `0` = the game's model lights as before (ENHANCEMENTS OFF). GPU (exclusive 4x M7, governor 0, `_AB`=30, 2 runs x 3 windows): +0.006 +-0.027 ms per stereo frame, the noise floor (a first version that copied the whole light block per pixel: +0.030) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_S` | `1.5` | `0.05`..`30` s | Cockpit scene light: time constant of the sky / horizon / ground bands (a band seen in fewer of its 5 patches learns more slowly) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_S@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_BOUNCE` | `0.55` | `0`..`4` | Cockpit scene light: the sun's light thrown about inside the cockpit, added to every facing of the dome: this x the key light's colour x the sun's height (sin of its elevation) x the share of the sun getting through (our clouds' shadow at the aircraft, inside a cloud). It keeps a sunlit cockpit's shade as bright as the game's high clear-day ambient had it (Tornado, same-frame A/B: M3 x1.07, M4 x1.02 the cockpit's mean linear luminance; without it x0.68 / x0.58, the F-1 in M4 x0.24) and fades under an overcast, in a storm, at dawn / dusk (a low sun) and at night (a dim key light). `0` = the sky dome alone | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_BOUNCE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_NIGHT` | `0` | `0`..`1` | Cockpit scene light at night (S5's night flag: M11): its strength there. `0` = the game's night lights stay -- they light the panel from below in the city's orange glow; the dome (an orange-brown murk, ~0.2) took the A-10's panel to ~0.74 of its brightness and contrast (display mean 17 -> 12.7, same-frame A/B) while the night cockpit already sat in its world (Tornado cockpit / world 0.22 before, 0.25 with it) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_SCENE_LIGHT_NIGHT@@ |
