A level is, per part, an index list over the part's own vertices -- no vertex moves, no new vertex: first the converter's 5 cm AO subdivision undone where the baked AO allows (the merged triangle interpolates uv and normal exactly as the pair did; level 1 within 2/255 of the AO, level 2 within 8/255), then meshoptimizer's edge collapses within 0.5 / 1.5 px of the 4x eye target at the part's nearest approach (its bounding sphere minus a 15 cm lean, at least 0.2 m), normals, texture coordinates and AO held in the same error (level 1: 3/255 AO, 0.08 normal, 0.5 texel; level 2: 0.03, 0.2, 2 texels). Small detail goes first (rounded caps, knurls, bolt heads' segments, the AO mesh on flat panels); glass, the hands and the screens are never touched. Every pass draws the level (the sun's shadow map, the depth pre-pass and its colour, the depth into the frame) except the mirrors' real view and the canopy's interior cube. Triangles drawn: of as built, level 1 / level 2: MiG-31 707k: 58 / 43 %, Rafale M 986k: 88 / 81 %, F-117A 155k: 68 / 56 %, F-5E 176k: 54 / 39 %, J35J 70k: 82 / 75 %; all 43 cockpit files 9.85 M: 68 / 59 %. The side file is 0.3-6 MB. Parts whose surfaces coincide with another part's within 0.05 mm keep the file's triangles at every level (the Rafale's split nodes: 36 parts, 474k triangles), since the GPU only sorts those by exact depth ties. Silhouette check (cpit_view -noglass, 5 views at the 4x target, 3.67 Mpx each): at most 99 pixels newly uncovered in a view. Only these five models were checked in the game's dumps; a model's first use at a lower level needs a look. No side file = the model as built (logged `no mesh LOD`); a side file of another build is refused (per-part triangle counts). Bit `1`: the solid parts without cut-out texels (their colour pass where the depth pre-pass's depth is equal); bit `2`: the glass (canopy, windscreen, combiner, dial glass: its scratches, dust and drops coarser off-axis). The cut-out parts (alpha test), the HUD screens and the depth passes never change. Done by the primitive shading rate of cockpit_vrs.vert (per triangle, by its provoking vertex's angle off the eye's axis) combined by MAX with the pass's crop image (PS2_VRS_FOV), so no other pipeline changes; the device's primitiveFragmentShadingRate is enabled only when this (or its A/B, its flip) asks for it. Zones at 89 deg (all 1x1): the re-draw equals the plain pipeline up to the re-draw floor (1 px by 1 level of 0.9 M, as the PS2_PERF_AB=2 control). GPU per stereo frame (exclusive 4x, in-run ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB, class timers; MiG-31 / Rafale M / F-117A): the glass (`2`) M4 sea -0.144 +- 0.005 / -0.205 +- 0.008 / -0.136 +- 0.006 ms of its 0.37 / 0.48 / 0.37 (whole frame with the solid bit: -0.175 / -0.240 / -0.193 +- 0.02), M1 overcast with the canopy wet -0.258 +- 0.010 / -0.373 +- 0.015 / -0.241 +- 0.010 of 0.67 / 0.87 / 0.67 (whole frame -0.299 / -0.404 / -0.310 +- 0.02; headset x1.75 ~ -0.5 / -0.7 / -0.5); the solid bit only -0.023 / -0.046 / -0.053 of the model's 0.87 / 1.06 / 0.48 (whole frame -0.02 / -0.06 / -0.07 +- 0.02): the dense models are bound by their small triangles (with a 1-pixel scissor 0.40-0.41 ms of the pass are left), which give as many coarse invocations as fine ones -- not worth its look. In-between frames save the same. Look (4x same-frame flips, the left eye's crop): glass only, dry (MiG-31 M4): 1.3-2.9 % of the pixels differ at all, <= 0.003 % by more than 8 levels; glass only, wet (Rafale M1): 0.12 % by more than 16 levels, the drops' refraction rims beyond ~40 deg soft and blocky; the solid bit: panel labels and dial text 30-50 deg off the axis smeared (4.6-5.4 % of those pixels by more than 16 levels; the centre identical). Not a default: ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY gives the glass the zones only while the canopy is dry (perf5_glasszones); bit 2 (glass) is the candidate for a headset look, bit 1 is not worth it; the desktop window, recordings (cine view) and eye dumps show the zones too | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_ZONES` | `30,40` | `r1,r2` degrees off the eye's axis (0..89) | (perf4_cockpit 2026-11-03) The rings of ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS: 1x1 inside r1, 2x1 / 1x2 between r1 and r2 (coarse along the radius, where the planar image has the most pixels per degree), 2x2 beyond r2 (at 4 samples the device's largest coarse fragment: 4x4 needs 64 coverage samples, the 3090 Ti takes 16). Wider rings keep more of the cockpit at full rate: the share of the shading work left is 43-46 % (solid) / 44-50 % (glass) at `30,40`, 51-55 / 50-62 % at `35,45`, 60-64 / 64-73 % at `40,50`, 73-75 / 78-84 % at `45,55` (tools/cockpit/cpit_view.c -zones, MiG-31 / Rafale / F-117A, ahead + panel views, the 4x target) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_ZONES@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY` | `0` (opt-in: a headset decision) | `1` | (perf5_glasszones 2026-11-03; the user agreed to shading zones on the dry canopy only) The glass's shading zones (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS bit 2's, rings ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_ZONES: 1x1 inside 30 deg off each eye's axis, 2x1 / 1x2 to 40, 2x2 beyond) only while nothing on the glass would show them; full rate otherwise. The gate shuts in the same frame as any of: water or frozen drops, mist, the condensation film, frost / rime (canopy_active()'s thresholds: below them nothing of it is drawn), a crack, a debris chip from a bit or a chunk (the crack layer: they stay for the mission), a debris fleck, or the sun lighting the glass's wear 10-85 deg off the view's axis (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY_SUN); it opens again after ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY_HOLD (2 s) without any. Soot / dust, grime / smear and a kill's grit pits leave it open. The pipelines are made at the cockpit's load, with PS2_PERF_GLASS_VARIANTS each variant's zone twin (cockpit_vrs vertex stage + the gx fragment variant; zones + twin = zones + plain shader on the glass byte for byte, the flip `gxv`): the two savings stack and the switch costs nothing in a frame. Never in the recordings' cinematic view. `0`: no primitive shading rate, no twins, nothing new in the frame. Look (exclusive 4x same-frame flips, zones vs none, Rafale M over M4's sea, the left eye's crop, % of the pixels > 8 levels): dry glass 0.0007-0.0031 %, soot 0.45 0.0006-0.0019 %, grime + smear 0.0005-0.0022 %, grit pits 38-44 deg off the axis 0.0001-0.0008 %: inside perf4_cockpit's dry bound, yet side by side in 4x crops the smallest wear beyond 30 deg is softer (dust specks 2x2 blobs instead of crisp dots, a 1-px scratch bit fainter or gone): why it is not a default. What shuts it: drops 0.30-0.41 %, the last drops (water 0.03) 0.023-0.029 %, frozen drops + rime 0.26-0.33 %, X-02S M18 0.018-0.21 %, cracks 0.20 %, a fleck 0.0077 %, the film's diffused world blocky (> 2 levels on 0.33 %), the sun 38-41 deg off the axis 0.043-0.050 % (its lit scratch streaks blocky). GPU: exclusive 4x in-run ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB (item cvrsd = this gate, cvrsg = the zones always; PS2_GPU_CLASSES=2, PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2, smooth layered, the census head script, no weapons), the glass class per frame against variants on, zones off, MiG-31 / F-117A over M4's dry sea: -0.050 +- 0.007 / -0.057 +- 0.008 ms (the gate open 81 % of those frames: the sun shut it while looking back up), -0.071 / -0.064 +- 0.004 while open (of 0.18 / 0.17); game and in-between frames alike, so -0.10 / -0.12 ms per 120 Hz pair (headset x1.75 ~ -0.18 / -0.20), -0.14 / -0.13 while open (~ -0.25 / -0.22). Rafale M: its run on the variants was disturbed (whole frame 11.0 ms against 8.3); against the plain shader -0.087 +- 0.010 / -0.121 +- 0.006, and the other two kept 0.8 of theirs on the variants: ~ -0.07 / -0.10, an estimate. The canopy wet (light rain) in the same runs: +0.007 / +0.010 +- 0.011-0.015: nothing. With ACZ_VR_SMOOTH_LAYER_COCKPIT=1 the in-between frames reuse a dry canopy's game-frame cockpit, so the saving counts in the game frames only. Log: `cockpit: dry-canopy gate open / shut ...` with the reason (the first 8 switches, then every 64th) and every 5 minutes its share of the frames. Untested in the headset | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY@@ |

| `ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB_WHAT` | `msaa2` | comma list of `msaa2`, `msaa4`, `cutpre`, `nocutpre`, `cvrs`, `cvrsg`, `cvrsa`, `cvrsd`, `tex`, `gxvoff`, `gwsnap`, `lod1`, `lod2`, `texb`, `cdmed`, `cdlow`, `cqmed`, `cqlow`, `cqa`..`cqd`; measurement only (wrong images): `gxa`..`gxf`, `nocpit`, `vx`, `nocomp`, `nodepth`, `noglass`, `nocut`, `noeq`, `noscr`, `nosm` | [measurement] The items of ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB: `msaa2` / `msaa4` the model at 2 / 4 samples (needs ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MSAA >= 4; the twins are made for it), `cutpre` / `nocutpre` ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_CUT_PREPASS on / off; `nocpit` no model pass at all (no multisampled pass, composite or depth; the veil and the scene light's copy stay), `vx` the model's passes with a 1-pixel scissor and no composite (what is left: vertex / primitive work, clear and resolve), `nocomp` no composite, `nodepth` no depth of the model into the frame (the HUD combiner's passes stay), `noglass` / `nocut` / `noeq` / `noscr` the multisampled pass without its glass / its parts with cut-out texels / the solid parts' colour (their depth pre-pass stays) / the HUD screens; `cvrs` / `cvrsg` / `cvrsa` the shading zones of ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS `1` / `2` / `3`, `cvrsd` the glass's zones while the canopy is dry (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_VRS_DRY's gate, whatever the switch says; perf5_glasszones 2026-11-03), `tex` the textures through the A/B's sampler (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB_ANISO / _LOD_BIAS) (perf4_cockpit 2026-11-03); `gxvoff` the plain glass pipeline (PS2_PERF_GLASS_VARIANTS off), `gwsnap` the canopy's world snapshot copy (PS2_PERF_CANOPY_INPLACE off), `gxa`..`gxf` the glass with the parts of ACZ_VR_GLASS_AB_MASKS left out; these items also apply in PS2_BENCH_REPEAT's extra drawings, so with PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2 a frame's saving is that of two drawings (= one 120 Hz game + in-between pair under layered smooth motion) (perf5_glassexact 2026-11-03). (perf6_cockpitladder 2026-11-04, ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_DETAIL's rungs) `lod1` / `lod2` = mesh LOD level 1 / 2 (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_LOD; the side file is read for them), `texb` = the textures through the budget's twins (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB_TEX_BUDGET), `cdmed` / `cdlow` = the medium / low level whole (its LOD level, the texture twins, 2 samples where the level has them), `nosm` = no sun shadow map (measurement only: no shadows). These items apply to the frame's own drawing, not to PS2_BENCH_REPEAT's extra ones, so a saving is that of one drawing; `cqmed` / `cqlow` / `cqa`..`cqd` the glass with that CANOPY QUALITY set in both drawings of a PS2_BENCH_REPEAT frame (ACZ_VR_CANOPY_QUALITY, ACZ_VR_CANOPY_QUALITY_AB_MASKS) | @@ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB_WHAT@@ |

Drawn with the G-vision veil (gforce.frag, its pipeline made also when ACZ_IMM_GLOC is off), only while the cockpit model is drawn; nothing is drawn while the way is clear. ## Sky, clouds and weather

Keeping Zero's sky, clouds and sun right in head-tracked frames (`runtime/src/zero_vr.c`, `runtime/src/ps2_video.c`). There are no weather-specific variables; `PS2_VRS` (coarse shading of the cloud sprites) is listed under the renderer.

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_HEAD` | on (with head tracking) | `0` | Build the cloud field and sky layers with the head-turned camera, so clouds do not follow the head in world-locked frames | @@ACZ_VR_CLOUD_HEAD@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_UPRIGHT` | on | `0`, `old` | Turn the cloud layer by the difference between the drawn roll and the roll the game placed the clouds with (0 with `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_HEAD`), and each sprite upright about its own centre (head roll plus the perspective tilt of verticals); `old` = the behaviour before 2026-10-20 (double roll, bug #18; debug A/B) | @@ACZ_VR_CLOUD_UPRIGHT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SKY_ANGLES` | on (with head tracking and `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_HEAD`) | `0` | Give the sky camera the head-turned angles during the sky draw, so the dome and horizon haze stay with the world in cockpit frames | @@ACZ_VR_SKY_ANGLES@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SUN_SCALE` | `1.0` | multiplier | Shrink the sun flare, glow and ghosts to the game's angular size, like the HUD | @@ACZ_VR_SUN_SCALE@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SKY_ROOT` | off | `1` (default root 0x1618A0) or a hex address | [experimental] Give recently head-turned view contexts their head-turned camera during the sky's frame draw | @@ACZ_VR_SKY_ROOT@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SKY_CAM` | on | `0` | Rebuild the sky camera struct's rotation-only matrices (+0xB0/+0xF0) from the head-turned view during the sky draw: the cloud deck/ceiling planes move with the world | @@ACZ_VR_SKY_CAM@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SKY_SITES` | off | `1` | [experimental] Also head-turn the extra camera updates for sky, haze and environment passes; no visible effect found | @@ACZ_VR_SKY_SITES@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_SHADOW_HEAD` | on in the PS2_RQ build (the Quest and the PC test build; the PC build has no such code) | `0` | (rq4_views 2026-11-11, BUGS_RQ R-97; the user's M10 third person, 201-217 s: "the aircraft's shadow follows me") The aircraft's soft shadow in head-tracked frames: its pass 0x235360 (called by the scene renderer 0x1D6EF8) makes a half-size (320 x 240) view context on the stack from the player camera's game values and updates it at 0x235734 / 0x235D34, then draws the aircraft's silhouette with it into a 256 x 224 target the frame subtracts from the screen 1:1 (R-51a). Not a flight site, it never got the head: the silhouette was drawn for the unturned camera with the game's 59 deg screen (d 313.9 for 320 px), so where the head turns the camera (the Quest's chase view) the shadow stayed where the unturned view had it, 2.7 times too large about the screen's centre -- a hard dark blade that moved with the head. With the switch the head's turn, position and screen go into those two updates (apply_head) and are given back after them; the frame's camera record and the head-camera table stay as they were. Logged once (`the shadow pass's view ... takes the head-turned camera`). `0` = the game's context. Not the sky sites (ACZ_VR_SKY_SITES=1 leaves the silhouette as it was) | @@ACZ_VR_SHADOW_HEAD@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_SKY` | off | any | [debug] Log the sky's view contexts, the swapped sky angles and camera rebuild deltas (from field 1500) | @@ACZ_DEBUG_SKY@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_ADDYAW` | off | radians | [debug] Add this much yaw to the head-turned sky angles (`ACZ_VR_SKY_ANGLES`) to exaggerate the effect | @@ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_ADDYAW@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_NEARMESH` | off | `1` | [debug] Log depth and Z saturation of near native meshes not detected as cockpit | @@ACZ_DEBUG_NEARMESH@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_YAW` | `0` | degrees | [debug] Turn the rebuilt sky matrices about the vertical axis (tests what depends on them) | @@ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_YAW@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_KEEP` | off | any | [debug] Leave the rebuilt sky camera in place after the draw | @@ACZ_DEBUG_SKY_KEEP@@ |
| `ACZ_DEBUG_CLOUD_UPRIGHT` | `0` | N | [debug] Log the cloud upright rotation every N XR frames | @@ACZ_DEBUG_CLOUD_UPRIGHT@@ |
| `PS2_DEBUG_SKIP_KIND` | `0` | `1` cloud sprites, `2` sky, `3` horizon haze, `4` horizon band | [debug] Drop one kind of display draw | @@PS2_DEBUG_SKIP_KIND@@ |
| `ACZ_VR_FX_ANGLES` | on | `0` | Give the effects camera (0x17E8A0: snow/rain particle box, billboards) the head-turned angles during its build, so the snow volume surrounds the gaze instead of the aircraft's nose | @@ACZ_VR_FX_ANGLES@@ |

| `ACZ_VR_CANOPY_QUALITY` | `high` (unset) | `high`, `medium`, `low`; the ini key `canopy_quality`, F4 > Enhancements > Expert (ini): HIGH (unset) / MEDIUM (`medium`) / LOW (`low`); the QUALITY PRESET sets it (a restart item) | (perf6_glassladder 2026-11-04; the rungs for the MEDIUM / LOW presets) `high` = the glass as before: no new pipeline, no primitive shading rate; frozen and optimised, the glass module's seven variants and the plain case are the same instructions as main's (tools_gl/spv_same.sh), same-frame flips `gxv` byte-identical at 4x. `medium` / `low` keep every part on the glass (water, frost and rime, film, mist, grime, soot, flecks, cracks, the wear) and shade it with less work. Both: the cheaper noise (cockpit.frag GXQ_*: the water's value noise on the ice's one-round hash; where the water gathers from three sines; the film from one noise octave + two sines with 3 blur taps instead of 6; grime and soot from one octave, no soot grain: other patterns, the same statistics; the drops stay in their cells), plus the glass's shading zones where the device has a primitive shading rate (the rings around each eye's axis: 1x1 inside, 2x1 / 1x2 to the second ring, 2x2 beyond; `medium` 30 / 40 deg, `low` 20 / 30 deg; not in the recordings' cinematic view). Beyond the rings small drops and dust specks are soft, a 1-px scratch fainter. Without a shading rate (GTX 10xx, RX 5xx class) only the noise saves. The rung's bits go into the variants' masks, so the exact savings stay. Only the multisampled pass's glass has rungs (COCKPIT ANTI-ALIASING OFF: plain glass); PS2_PERF_GLASS_VARIANTS=0: high. Load: 10 more pipelines at a cockpit's load when a rung is configured (20 with the 2-sample twins the governor asks for), none at high. Measured (simulator on the 3090 Ti, exclusive, the user's settings, governor off, PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2, in-run ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_AB items `cqmed` / `cqlow`, ms per 120 Hz pair, glass class): M1 overcast, natural weather, HIGH -> medium / low saving, 4x: MiG-31 1.29 -> -0.65 / -0.78, Rafale M 1.62 -> -0.87 / -1.03, F-117A 1.26 -> -0.60 / -0.73; X-02S M18 0.67 -> -0.33 / -0.40; 3x medium MiG-31 0.78 -> -0.38, Rafale M 0.97 -> -0.51; 2x low MiG-31 0.43 -> -0.24, Rafale M 0.49 -> -0.29; inside the presets (ACZ_QUALITY_PRESET, F-5E, M1): MEDIUM 3x 0.61 -> -0.31 (the whole GPU pair 4.15 ms, -7.5 %), LOW 2x 0.32 -> -0.17 (2.60 ms, -6.7 %). Forced states, Rafale M 4x: dry 0.47 -> -0.20 / -0.25, light rain 1.05 -> -0.52 / -0.60, heavy rain + mist 1.18 -> -0.55 / -0.68, frozen drops + rime 1.35 -> -0.65 / -0.85, film + mist 1.38 -> -0.80 / -0.96, grime + smear 0.97 -> -0.49 / -0.59, grime + soot + flecks 1.41 -> -0.82 / -0.94, dry + cracks 0.80 -> -0.35 / -0.45. The shader parts alone (no shading rate): dry and cracks 0, rain -0.09, frost -0.11, film -0.39, grime -0.14, grime + soot -0.36. No terrain pack in these runs. The headset is not measured: x1.15-1.75 of the simulator's figures (disputed). NOTES_ZERO_VR.md perf6_glassladder has the table per aircraft and state | @@ACZ_VR_CANOPY_QUALITY@@ |

Each lights only where it scatters the sun towards the eye: a line where its tangent is square to the sun-eye geometry, so the lit hairlines line up on circles around the sun's image (the halo of a worn windscreen) and a swirl lights as a streak through its middle pointing at the sun; forward scatter falling off with the angle from the sun (lines ~11 deg, specks ~16 deg e-fold; looked up within 23 deg, faded out from 17); nothing with the sun behind the glass, none below the horizon; dimmed by our clouds' shadow at the aircraft and inside cloud; hidden where water, condensation film or frost cover the glass. This definitely needs fixing", 22:52:42 "the mirrors still need fixing") What stands behind the pilot in the mirrors -- the headrest, the canopy's frame and rails, the spine and fins -- drawn for real instead of marched through a cube: a flat mirror shows the scene from the eye's mirror image E' = E - 2 ((E - c) . n) n, so every frame (in-between frames too: the eyes move) and for each eye and each mirror within ~15 deg of the view, cockpit.vert draws the model from E' with the glass's own axes as the camera (x along the glass, y = n x x, looking through it along n) and a projection that lays the glass's extent onto the mirror's slot of an atlas at k texels a metre (texel = k (u - u0), k (v1 - v): the glass reads it by its own point, cockpit.frag mirv_look; the plane is the glass's centre with the aimed normal, ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MIRRORS_AIM), the near plane at the glass (what lies behind the mirror is clipped); the same lighting as the cockpit's solid parts (the game's light block, the scene light, the sun's shadow map, flashes, the cloud light), 4x multisampled and resolved (ACZ_VR_COCKPIT_MIRRORS_REAL_MSAA), alpha = coverage over the far scene (sky, our clouds, the live map). The parts are culled by bounding spheres -- at load the solid parts that may stand in front of each mirror, every part also in chunks of 32 triangles (file order) and groups of 16 chunks -- once for each eye and mirror and kept while that eye stays within 5 mm (a margin for it), into runs of chunks a draw; parts an animation moves are tested every view (the renderer's recording: 0.056 ms a view, F-15C, all three mirrors; one culling ~0.15 ms). The cube march drew the F-15C top mirror's view over the headrest (47 % of its rays meet a part at its +3 deg aim) as terraced, stair-stepped streaks 3-4 eye pixels wide, different in each eye and changing with every millimetre of head motion (head drifting 0.2 mm a frame: pixels changing by more than 16 levels from frame to frame 0.54 / 0.88 % of the glass with the march, 0.18 / 0.24 % with the real view; by more than 32: 0.04 / 0.10 % against 0.00 / 0.00 %). | `ACZ_VR_FX_BURST` | `1` | `0` = the game's glow as before; strength `0.1`..`2` (ENHANCEMENTS > PICTURE > EXPLOSIONS: SOFT WITH VOLUMES / OFF) | (fx_burst 2026-11-02, bug #266: M18 X-02 trailer runs, "the huge explosion Pixy releases ... a very harsh gradient; it does not look volumetric, it still looks 2D; there is no beautiful explosion gradient") Pixy's MPBM burst (M18's second phase: his detonation 0x2216A4 makes the 0x180300 set with effect 102, seen with nothing else) becomes a volume marched in true stereo where the game's burst is (burst.vert / burst.frag after the world and its effects, with the trails): a turbulent shell whose lumps ride the blast outwards, white-hot in the middle cooling through yellow, orange and deep red into smoke (a piecewise-linear black-body ramp, no flat bands at its stops), soft edges, each eye's own ray, ended at the scene's depth and faded by our clouds' transmittance in front where the effects' cloud veil is bound (ACZ_VR_CLOUD_FX_SOFT, multiview), else by the frame's depth test at the sphere's front; 22 jittered steps a pixel, dithered output. Faithful timing and size: the game draws the burst as one big quad of an 8 x 8 texel glow (atlas texels u 248..255, v 193..200) split into up to ~16 columns plus a copy into its glow target (blurred, reduced to 1/8 and laid back over the frame: the blocky lavender halo with the stair-stepped edge); each game frame the frame's columns give the radius (R = d sin(0.9 x the quad's half height about the burst's centre)) and the strength (the columns' alpha: 255 for ~3.2 s, then e^(-(t - 3.2) / 0.9 s)); while they do not show, fitted curves (R = 1120 m (1 - 0.55 e^(-t / 1.6 s)) scaled to the last measurement). The heat follows the game's alpha (white-hot while it is full, deep red as it fades); as it fades the volume dissipates (its thin parts first). Its point flash and hit flashes stay as before. GPU (exclusive 4x, ACZ_VR_FX_BURST_AB, frames with a burst): M18 +0.01..+0.25 ms, mean +0.15 per stereo frame; the eye inside a test burst +0.30..+0.49 (ACZ_VR_FX_BURST_RATE); nothing without a burst. | `ACZ_VR_CLOUD_WAKE` | `1` | `0` = off, strength `0.1`..`2` (menu: ON 1, SUBTLE 0.5, OFF) | The cloud wake (2026-10-29, agent cl_wake; docs/research/2026-10-29/cloud-wake.md; zero_trails.c, ps2_clouds_wake.c + cloud_wake.comp, the trails pass `trl_*`, trails.frag): leaving one of our volumetric clouds (needs ACZ_VR_CLOUDS near / all), every aircraft the game flies drags out a short torn veil of the cloud in its vortex wake (1.8 spans wide, widening 2.4 m/s with ACZ_VR_CLOUD_WAKE_LOOK 2; 1.4 / 1.4 before, at the edge about as opaque as ~15 m of real cloud, thinning over ACZ_VR_CLOUD_WAKE_DRAG metres past the cloud's edge) and, in the humid shell around the cloud or in a pull, its two vortex cores condense into thin threads (1 g: 40-120 m; >= 2 g: up to ~600 m, 400 with ACZ_VR_CLOUD_WAKE_LOOK=1). Both sink with the wake (1.8 m/s x the load factor, against the lift, until the vortex pair links after ~4 t0: ~25-30 m), widen, the threads meander (Crow), and everything breaks up and evaporates in the time a 12 um droplet needs in the mixed air (0.85 s / (1 - RH): 7-10 s in mission 3). Inside / outside from a GPU probe of our clouds' own density at each aircraft (up to 32 within ACZ_VR_CLOUD_WAKE_RANGE, ~3 game frames late, asked 0.35 s ahead and held 0.35 s over the clear pockets inside a cloud). World strips in true stereo through the contrail pass (lit with the game's cloud palette and our cloud shadow map, behind terrain, aircraft and our clouds' stamped depth). Both re-draws then run our passes on the same inputs and a flip's difference is the flip's alone. Before, every re-draw re-read C1 and updated the maps: the PS2_PERF_AB=2 control differed by 1-3 levels over whole cloud banks (M1 in the overcast: 20-330 k of 0.9 M px). A rung changes only the near volume (4-600 m: the in-cloud veil and its lumps, near cloud edges); the far map beyond 600 m, its composite, the shadow map, the optics and the wake stay as they are. Levers: `div` = the near buffer's texel covers div x div target pixels (HIGH 2: half resolution per axis), `step` / `grow` / `tier` = ACZ_VR_CLOUD_NEAR_STEP / _GROW / _TIER, `detail` = ACZ_VR_CLOUD_NEAR_DETAIL. `medium` = div 3, `low` = div 4 (not step 12.5: near march -71 % instead of -58 %, but the two plane families' seam and the plane contours show in thin cloud against the sky, up to ~15 levels). An explicitly set ACZ_VR_CLOUD_NEAR_* switch wins on every rung. The near images are made for the smallest divisor in use (at 4x 18.3 MB -> 8.1 / 4.6 MB); the in-between near reuse and the coarse periphery run at divisor 2 only. GPU per drawing (sim, exclusive 4x, user settings, layered, governor off, PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2, in-run ACZ_VR_CLOUD_DETAIL_AB, against HIGH with mean +- SE, game / in-between frames): medium M1 overcast -0.243 +- 0.017 / -0.240 +- 0.016 ms (cloud passes -25 / -33 %), M18 -0.053 +- 0.028 / -0.185 +- 0.033, M3 -0.015 +- 0.014 (cloud passes -7 %), M12 -0.035 +- 0.018; low M1 -0.387 +- 0.040 / -0.422 +- 0.028 (cloud passes -33 / -49 %), M18 -0.102 +- 0.027 / -0.254 +- 0.067, M3 -0.032 +- 0.010 (cloud passes -8 %), M12 -0.046 +- 0.022. Per 120 Hz pair in M1's overcast -0.48 / -0.81 ms (headset x1.75 ~-0.85 / -1.4). Look: same frame against HIGH (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=clouddetail): mean absolute difference over the eye's visible box at 4x, medium / low: M1 overcast 0.008 / 0.022 levels, through an M3 cumulus 0.008 / 0.011 (max 14 / 5), M18 0.007 / 0.017, cloud edges against the sky and the canopy frame included. Directions at infinity (halo, rainbow) are the same in both eyes; glory and spectre sit on the cloud surface per eye. Day only, none inside cloud, every condition fades over ~1 s, no screen-space history. Needs our far clouds (`ACZ_VR_CLOUDS=all` or `far`). ## Renderer, upscaling and performance

### Resolution, presentation and timing

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_UPSCALE` | F4 setting (`play_zero_vr.sh`: `3`; its sharp mode: ENHANCEMENTS RESOLUTION, `4`) | `0` = Auto, `1`..`8` | Internal resolution multiplier (capped by the GPU's image size limit); overrides the setting | @@PS2_UPSCALE@@ |
| `PS2_FPS_CAP` | F4 setting | fps; `<=0` = no limit | Presentation frame-rate cap, overrides the setting | @@PS2_FPS_CAP@@ |
| `PS2_PRESENT_MODE` | F4 setting (mailbox) | `fifo`, `mailbox`, `immediate`, `relaxed` | Vulkan present mode of the window | @@PS2_PRESENT_MODE@@ |
| `PS2_ASPECT` | F4 setting | float, e.g. `1.3333` | Force the displayed aspect ratio | @@PS2_ASPECT@@ |
| `PS2_FIELD_HZ` | NTSC 59.94 Hz (`play_zero_vr.sh`: `60` in VR) | Hz (1..10000) | Vblank field clock; 60 makes 60 fps line up with a 120 Hz headset (game runs 0.1% fast) | @@PS2_FIELD_HZ@@ |
| `PS2_LOCKSTEP` | off (gsreplay: on) | non-0 / `0` | Renderer waits for every field and never drops one (deterministic output) | @@PS2_LOCKSTEP@@ |
| `PS2_ASYNC_GFX` | on | `0` | Graphics machine (VIF, VU1, GIF, GS) on its own thread; `0` keeps it on the EE thread. While a DMA-level GS capture (capture.on / F6, level dma) is wanted or recording, the EE drains this queue at the end of every field and writes the capture's field records, start and stop itself (bug #111: they used to come from the worker, up to two fields behind, so such captures lost their first field's records and were torn by two unsynchronised writers); GS-level captures stay with the worker; nothing changes without a capture | @@PS2_ASYNC_GFX@@ |
| `PS2_ASYNC_MB` | `64` | MB, `1`..`1024` | Size of the async graphics ring buffer | @@PS2_ASYNC_MB@@ |
| `PS2_ASYNC_FIELDS` | `2` | `1`..`8` | How many fields the async graphics queue may run ahead | @@PS2_ASYNC_FIELDS@@ |
| `PS2_GFX_SPLIT` | on (since 2026-10-25, ov_cpu) | `0` | The graphics worker in two stages (op_threads 2026-10-23): this thread runs the ring and the VIF1 command stream (codes, UNPACK) and forwards everything else in stream order through a second ring to a second thread, which runs the VU1 programs (native decoders), the GIF, the GS and the field's present at the same point of the stream (UNPACK writes as VU1 memory records before each MSCAL/MSCNT, MPG and DIRECT data, every other record verbatim; syncs at a VIF1 interrupt, a mode change and the EE's drain). Same work, same order, same results (replays of one capture: identical signatures and images; PS2_GFX_SPLIT_VERIFY). Sim in-run A/B: the critical stage's busy time per field -16 % (M3 heavy) / -24 % (M4), -27 % on top of op_stream's decode pool (M3 heavy 5.80 -> 4.21 ms), +0.8 ms CPU in all, +0.03-0.05 ms from the field's end to its publication, EE +0.4-1.3 ms; with the worker pinned to E-cores a ~3.6 ms publication tail on a quarter of the fields (THREADS_RESEARCH_2026-10-23.md). On by default since ov_cpu's in-run A/B in the user's settings (2026-10-25): M4 critical stage 5.16 -> 3.91 ms a field (-1.24 +- 0.08, p99 -1.13), M9 -0.99 +- 0.34, EE +0.76 ms, recording +0.04 ms, frame latency n.s., publication +0.02 ms (p99 +0.06); `0` = one worker (the headset's `speed: graphics stage 2` lines show it) | @@PS2_GFX_SPLIT@@ |
| `PS2_GFX_SPLIT_AB` | off | seconds | [diagnostic] In-run A/B of PS2_GFX_SPLIT: two stages in odd blocks of that many seconds, one worker in the even ones (switched at a field after stage 2 has finished; PS2_THREAD_PROF event 15 marks the blocks) | @@PS2_GFX_SPLIT_AB@@ |
| `PS2_GFX_SPLIT_VERIFY` | off | `1` | [test] With PS2_GFX_SPLIT: every VU1 memory record carries a hash of the lanes stage 1 wrote; stage 2 re-reads them after applying and logs differences (`gfx-split verify:`) | @@PS2_GFX_SPLIT_VERIFY@@ |
| `PS2_PIPELINE_CACHE` | `<exe dir>/ac5_pipelines` | path prefix; `0` = off | Vulkan pipeline cache (`.keys` / `.cache`), so later runs build pipelines at start-up instead of stuttering | @@PS2_PIPELINE_CACHE@@ |
| `PS2_PIPE_WARM_THREADS` | `4` (`1` with PS2_THREADS=quest) | `0`..`8` | Worker threads that build the remembered pipelines at start-up (`0` = renderer thread in 4 ms slices) | @@PS2_PIPE_WARM_THREADS@@ |
| `PS2_PIPE_CACHE_COMPACT` | on | `0` | `ac5_pipelines.cache` gets our own header (shader-set stamp from the `.spv` names / sizes / times, blob size and FNV-1a 64) and starts EMPTY when the shaders changed, the file has no header (older builds), fails its size / hash check or exceeds `PS2_PIPE_CACHE_MAX_MB`; the start-up warm-up rebuilds it from the remembered keys (Vulkan cannot drop cache entries; the driver blob kept every old shader version: 31.3 MB for 246 states -> 4.7 MB). Also keeps remembered keys of features that are off this session (foveated bit 52, dynamic blend bit 53) in `.keys`. `0` = the old behaviour (plain blob, any valid one loaded) | @@PS2_PIPE_CACHE_COMPACT@@ |
| `PS2_PIPE_CACHE_MAX_MB` | `32` | MB; `0` = no limit | With `PS2_PIPE_CACHE_COMPACT`: a cache blob larger than this starts empty (rebuilt by the warm-up); the file reader refuses 64 MB | @@PS2_PIPE_CACHE_MAX_MB@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_PIPE_SAVE_ASYNC` | on | `0` | The periodic pipeline-cache save during play (20 s after new pipeline states appeared) on a short-lived background thread (the renderer copies the key list only): vkGetPipelineCacheData, the hash and the two file writes held the renderer thread 8.5-16.9 ms between two attempts (0.05 ms now); the same files and bytes; the save at exit stays synchronous (ov_cpu 2026-10-25) | @@PS2_PERF_PIPE_SAVE_ASYNC@@ |
| `PS2_VB_DEVICE` | off | `1` | Vertex buffers in device-local, host-visible (ReBAR) memory instead of system RAM | @@PS2_VB_DEVICE@@ |

### GPU features and GS emulation

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_GS_MIPS` | off | `1` | Mip chains for GS textures: less shimmer, but costs spikes because Zero re-uploads atlases while the head turns | @@PS2_GS_MIPS@@ |
| `PS2_VRS` | on if the GPU supports it | `0` | Coarse (variable-rate) shading for the cloud sprites | @@PS2_VRS@@ |
| `PS2_VRS_RATE` | `2` | `2` or `4` | Coarse shading block: 2x2 or 4x4 pixels | @@PS2_VRS_RATE@@ |
| `PS2_VRS_FOV` | `crop` (VR stereo, if the GPU has attachment shading rates) | `0`/`off`, `crop`/`1`, `zones`/`2` | Foveated shading through a VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate attachment per eye layer (op_vrs 2026-10-23). Each eye layer is the whole symmetric image but the headset shows only that eye's crop (Quest 3 and the simulator: L x 0..1649, R x 399..2048, both y ~280..1792 of 2048x1792: 32 % of every layer is drawn and never shown). `crop`: that part is shaded once per 4x4 pixels (world, HUD, edge AA, the cockpit's MSAA pass); the crop itself is shaded exactly as before. `zones`: also the world draws (class 1) in rings around each eye's optical axis (PS2_VRS_FOV_ZONES); HUD, text, target boxes, the cockpit model, its screens and the edge AA stay 1x1. `0` = the old pipelines, no attachment. Every pipeline of ps2_video.c gets the attachment flag when it is on (the first start after a change recompiles the pipeline cache) | @@PS2_VRS_FOV@@ |
| `PS2_VRS_FOV_ZONES` | `30,40,50` | `r1,r2,r3` degrees | `zones`: 1x1 within r1 of the eye's axis, 2x1 left/right and 1x2 above/below (coarse along the radius) to r2, 2x2 to r3, 4x4 beyond (by attachment texel: 16x16 px on the RTX 3090 Ti, the texel's nearest point decides) | @@PS2_VRS_FOV_ZONES@@ |
| `PS2_VRS_FOV_CENTER` | `0,0` | `x,y` degrees | `zones`: the rings' centre moved off each eye's axis (x toward the nose, y up), for the headset check of where the lens is sharp | @@PS2_VRS_FOV_CENTER@@ |
| `PS2_VRS_FOV_DUMP_CROP` | off | `1` | Eye dumps (PS2_XR_DUMP_EYES) get the crop's 4x4 outside the eye crop too (default: dump frames keep the whole image 1x1 outside the zones, as our clouds do, so harness images stay complete) | @@PS2_VRS_FOV_DUMP_CROP@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK` | on (`cpit,eaa,cloud,copy`; `cloud` acts only with a lens mask) | `0`, `1`, or a list of `cpit`, `eaa`, `cloud`, `copy` | Pixels no eye sees kept out of our own passes (ov_passes 2026-10-25; never the game's): each eye's visible area = its crop of the symmetric layer (or the runtime's visible-area mesh, XR_KHR_visibility_mask) grown by PS2_PASS_MASK_MARGIN, the rest hidden. `cpit`: the cockpit's 4x MSAA pass renders only the union of the eyes' visible boxes (the top band of ~13 % of the layer is not cleared, drawn or resolved) and its depth is pre-filled with the nearest value over each eye's hidden area (pmask.vert, per view): the model's depth pre-pass and colour pass fail there by early-Z; the composite covers the visible mesh. `eaa`: edge AA covers each eye's visible mesh. `copy`: the eye copies to the headset take only the eye's crop (the imageRect the layer submits) and a margin of w / 64 px instead of the whole layer. `cloud` (only with a lens mask: with the crop alone the composites' own crop test discards as cheaply, +0.012 ms measured): the cloud composites cover the visible mesh and the near march skips the lens' hidden 16x16 px blocks. Outside the visible area the layer keeps the frame without cockpit / edge AA: never shown by the headset; the desktop window (which shows the right eye's whole layer) is cleared to black there (PS2_PASS_MASK_WINDOW), so it shows exactly what that eye sees. Sim (exclusive 4x, user settings, governor off, in-run A/B in 60-frame blocks): M3 J35J -0.035 / -0.043 ms per stereo frame (2 runs; blocks -0.021..-0.064; game and in-between frames alike), M4 F-1 -0.005 (inside its +-0.05 block noise). The crop the headset shows: the same-frame re-draw with the masks off differs by <= 7 levels on ~1 % of it, only in our cloud bank, as with an unrelated flip (re-draw noise). The lens path was exercised with PS2_PASS_MASK_TEST_LENS (corners masked, the rest as with the crop alone); the runtime's real mesh is untested (no headset). Eye dumps keep the whole image unless PS2_PASS_MASK_DUMP=1; exact image A/B PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=pmask, GPU A/B PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=mask | @@PS2_PASS_MASK@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK_WINDOW` | on | `0` | PS2_PASS_MASK: the desktop window shows the right eye's whole symmetric layer; where the masks left out the cockpit and edge AA (outside that eye's visible box: at 1920x1009 a strip x 0..343 and the band y 0..135, ~29 % of the window) it is cleared to black, so the window shows what the eye sees instead of a cockpit cut off at the crop. The recordings' scenes (OBS game capture, every collection) crop the window to the right eye at l374 t163, inside the box (31 / 28 px to spare): unchanged; the top-left FPS inset (200x44) shows the counter on black. Cost ~0 (a clear of the window's strips). `0` = the masked frame as it is (no cockpit / edge AA there) | @@PS2_PASS_MASK_WINDOW@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK_MARGIN` | `32` | pixels at 4x (scaled with PS2_UPSCALE) | PS2_PASS_MASK: how far the visible area reaches past each eye's crop / lens mesh (edge-AA taps reach 17 px; the compositor's filter and Link's sharpening read a few pixels past the crop) | @@PS2_PASS_MASK_MARGIN@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK_DUMP` | off | `1` | [test] PS2_PASS_MASK also in eye-dump frames (the dump then shows the masked layer; with PS2_PERF_AB=1 PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=pmask the `_nc` re-draw is the unmasked same frame) | @@PS2_PASS_MASK_DUMP@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK_TEST_LENS` | off | fraction `0.05`..`0.9` | [test] Without a runtime mask: cut each eye's crop corners as a lens would (triangles with legs = this fraction of the half width / height), to exercise the lens path (cockpit pre-fill, visible meshes, the near march's hidden blocks) on the simulator | @@PS2_PASS_MASK_TEST_LENS@@ |
| `PS2_PASS_MASK_LOG` | off (6 lines) | `1` | [test] `pass-mask:` lines (each eye's visible box, hidden share, union, vertices; the near march's hidden blocks) whenever the masks change | @@PS2_PASS_MASK_LOG@@ |
| `PS2_DATE_LOCAL` | on if supported | `0` | Destination alpha test reads the target in place (dynamic rendering local read); `0` goes back to copies. Native meshes that also write alpha only when flat (PS2_DATE_LOCAL_QUAD) | @@PS2_DATE_LOCAL@@ |
| `PS2_DATE_SNAP_EVERY` | off | `1` | One target snapshot per DATE draw instead of one shared by a run of them (old behaviour) | @@PS2_DATE_SNAP_EVERY@@ |
| `PS2_DATE_LOCAL_QUAD` | on | `0` | (ov_date 2026-10-25) Native-mesh draws with the destination alpha test (DATE) that also write alpha read the target in place too (PS2_DATE_LOCAL) when they are flat: up to 16 triangles in one plane that do not overlap there (an edge of one separates each pair; shared edges by equal positions), the eye well off the plane (more than its stereo shift and, in in-between frames, its motion since the game frame), no sliver on screen (corners >= 1/8 PS2 px off the opposite sides); in-between frames of unmatched meshes (screen-space path) keep the copy. Such a draw covers no pixel twice, so no fragment can read alpha the same draw wrote, and the in-place read gives exactly the pre-draw alpha the snapshot copy gave. Before, each one stopped the rendering for a snapshot copy of its box (two barriers, a copy, a restart): M4 over the sea draws its sea tiles in 5 passes, the 4th (tex 4, Cd - Cs*FIX, DATE "bit 7 clear", z + alpha written) one quad per tile, 40-60 a stereo frame. M4 sea capture (flat replay, per frame): snapshots 51 -> 10, begin-rendering 93 -> 53, barrier calls 215 -> 135, 0.72 M PS2 px of copies -> 0; 41 of 44 such draws read in place (the rest: 2 x 2 tiles not in one plane, kept). GPU (exclusive 4x, the user's settings, our clouds, governor off, in-run A/B PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=date in 60-frame blocks, paired blocks, 3 runs): M4 MiG-29A 40 m over the coast / port -0.32 / -0.34 / -0.34 (+-0.055) ms per stereo frame, over the sea -0.73 / -0.74 / -0.75 (+-0.035) (game and in-between frames alike; 5.12 -> 4.38 ms); M3 has no such draws (0 a frame: no change). Exact: gsreplay of a DMA capture over the M4 sea byte-identical on / off at fields 100, 200, 300 (and M3 captures); same-frame A/B (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=datequad) at the re-draw noise floor of PS2_PERF_AB=2. `0` = the copies as before; counters in the vk-count line (PS2_SPEED_LOG: date-alpha-meshes, why kept) | @@PS2_DATE_LOCAL_QUAD@@ |
| `PS2_DATE_BATCH` | `3` (since perf4_passes 2026-11-03; nx_date: `2`) | `0`, `1`, `2` | (nx_date 2026-10-25) DATE local-read feedback barriers batched. A DATE draw that reads the target in place (PS2_DATE_LOCAL) takes a feedback barrier whenever alpha was written into the target since the last one; the game draws its sea and terrain tile by tile in 3-5 passes (pass 1 writes alpha (FBA), a later DATE pass reads it), so every tile paid one (flat replays of DMA captures: 55.7 a frame over the M4 sea, 235 at the M14 sea peak, 734 in the M2 intro). `2`: consecutive native-mesh tiles (draws with bit-equal triangles = one tile's passes) all in one plane are re-issued pass-major (the 1st draw of every tile, then the 2nd, ...) when no pixel can belong to two tiles in any eye or in-between view: triangles of different tiles pairwise separated in the plane (an edge separates each pair; contacts only at equal positions; diagonal neighbours touching at one vertex by their angular wedges, in the plane and >= 0.05 rad on screen), the same view (block matrix, offsets, eye shift, in-between matrix), date_quad_ok's guards (eye off the plane by > 2 x (stereo shift + in-between camera motion) and 1e-3 of the distance to every tile, no sliver: corners >= 1/8 PS2 px off), never across one of our own passes (clouds, cockpit, edge AA, trails, depth snapshot), no cockpit / HUD-block / MFD / house / self-reading / colour-clip / overlay draws, not in the synchronous second stereo pass. Each pixel then still sees its own tile's draws in their order, and a DATE draw of a run takes a barrier only when its own tile wrote alpha since the last one: one per pass group instead of one per tile; the grouping also halves the pipeline binds. `1` (test only): instead a per-target box of the alpha writes since the last barrier (game frames), a DATE draw whose box misses it skipping the barrier: 0-3 a frame for +0.45-0.65 ms of recording in the M2 intro, not part of `2`. The in-between frames and the A/B re-draws reuse the game frame's runs. `3`: also heightfield runs (tiles not in one plane, e.g. M2's 2 x 2 terrain cells: their triangles cover a convex domain once, every eye on the same side of every triangle) -- in the M2 intro feedback barriers 733 -> 590 but GPU -0.08 ms for latency +0.3 ms (builder), so not by default. Replays (flat, 4x): feedback barriers M4 55.7 -> 23.7, M14 234.7 -> 41.5, M2 intro unchanged (`3`: 734 -> 588); barrier calls 137 -> 105 / 325 -> 133; pipeline binds M4 253 -> 158, M14 679 -> 324; byte-identical images at fields 60-300 of all three captures in modes 0 / 1 / 2 / 3. GPU per stereo frame (exclusive 4x, the user's settings + our clouds, governor off, in-run A/B PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=datebatch in 60-frame blocks, paired, no class timers; final build): M4 MiG-29A at 40 m over the coast / port -0.158 +- 0.031 ms, over the sea -0.279 +- 0.032 (earlier builds with the box / heightfield runs: -0.16 / -0.28 twice), latency -0.15 / -0.28; M14 A-10A low over the sea -0.22 +- 0.04 before the peak and -0.60 +- 0.14 at the sea peak (fields 1900-2200, 2 runs pooled), latency -0.14 / -0.37, unchanged after it; M2 with the intro: no change (intro -0.018 +- 0.005, flight +-0.01; latency n.s.). Same-frame A/B (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=datebatch, our clouds / immersion off): game and in-between frames 0 px over the M4 sea and the M14 sea peak (control PS2_PERF_AB=2: in-between frames 0.002-0.4 % at the re-draw floor). The M4 gain is above nx_census' ceiling for leaving out all feedback barriers (-0.09..-0.10): most of it is the halved pipeline / state changes of the pass-major order. Builder on the renderer thread 0.04 ms per game-frame pass in M4 and the M2 intro, 0.35 ms at the M14 sea peak (replay recording +0.15 there; in game the latency still drops). `0` = one barrier per tile in the game's draw order. Counters: the vk-date line (feedback barriers) and the vk-count date-batch line (PS2_SPEED_LOG: runs, why runs ended, builder time, box skips); PS2_DATE_BATCH_TRACE=N: frame N's runs (dbt-run lines) **Default `3` since perf4_passes (2026-11-03)**: in-run A/B of `3` against `2` (PS2_DATE_BATCH_AB_BASE=2, PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=datebatch, exclusive 4x, the user's settings, governor off, 60-frame blocks, perf4_timeline's scenes): M3 J35J GPU -0.114 +- 0.015 ms per stereo frame, frame latency -0.088 +- 0.019 (100 pairs, p99 4.49 -> 4.35); M1 overcast -0.061 +- 0.015 / -0.052 +- 0.018; M18 X-02S -0.060 +- 0.017 / -0.023 +- 0.024 (57 pairs); M2 Su-27 with the intro -0.023 +- 0.011 / -0.009 +- 0.015; the builder 0.03-0.04 ms a pass in that M2 run, 0.13-0.14 in M3 flight (light runs); M3 feedback barriers 52 -> 25 a frame, pipeline binds ~200 -> 110-175 (light runs). Walls: the foot's darkening in the lowest metres (contact with the ground, the street's occlusion) instead of the whole-wall gradient, the mission's low sun (M6: 8 deg) reaching the lower floors less, whole bays of windows between 0.7 m corner piers up to the cornice with frames, sills, the lintel's shadow and glass = the dark room mixed with the sky's (the game's fog colour's) reflection by the view angle (Schlick), varied per window, a faint trace under the sills, a 2 m plaster noise, a calm hue per building, a cornice band under flat roofs / the eaves' shadow under pitched ones; x0.90 so a wall's mean stays as before. World-fixed (both eyes, in-between frames), every detail faded into its mean under ~3 pixels: far rows are unchanged (same frame, 100 m pass: rows of the horizon band identical within 8 levels; nearer differing pixels 0.96 / 0.88 of the old mean luminance: the glossy roof highlights gone). The building's numbers ride in the records zero_props.c writes only when on (half length / width in quadword 1 w bits 16-31, 0.5 m steps; the wall's top and foot in the position's w, 1/16 m, + 1024 for a pitched roof; roofs as kinds 3 flat / 4 pitched with their corners' local position along the length / width in quadword 1 x / y, m x 16): the same vertex count, no CPU cost. The variant tests depth early (a building behind another is not shaded); the city's draws inherit the terrain pass's alpha test (alpha > 0.75: fragment flags 02276068) but are opaque buildings on land texels, so the variant never discards them. GPU (exclusive 4x in-run A/B ACZ_TERRAIN_CITY_LOOK_AB=10, M6 150 m passes over the residential districts, head 20 deg down, HUD view, governor off): the look +0.084 +- 0.007 / +0.085 +- 0.008 ms per stereo frame over the city (2 runs, 10 blocks of 400 frames each, frames ~2.5 ms; ~0.15 ms on the headset); the whole city on / off (ACZ_TERRAIN_PROPS_AB, with the look's previous build) +0.223 +- 0.024 / +0.229 +- 0.052. The first version in the base shader (no far path, late depth tests, four-hash noises) cost +0.2..+0.6. `PS2_PERF_AB=1 PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=citylook` = the same frame in the plain look | @@ACZ_TERRAIN_CITY_LOOK@@ |

Mean colour unchanged (box exact). The packs (one PNG per tile set, 22 sets for the 25 maps, 10-40 MB each) are game-derived and never in git: `ACZ_TERRAIN_TEXPACK_DIR`/<name>/t5_<CRC>_<nt>.png, found by the CRC-32 of the map's atlas + palette (a map without a pack file keeps the game's texture). Loading: the pack is decoded on a lowest-priority worker once the map is stable (sim: PNG decode 0.18-0.43 s, box mips + staging 11-29 ms; 30 stable frames first, as the water) and uploaded in chunks of `ACZ_TERRAIN_TEXPACK_CHUNK` layers per frame; until then, and on the frame the map changes, the game's texture. Memory: 85 MB of VRAM (RGBA8, 1024 layers, all levels; made at start when on) and an 85 MB host staging buffer; the upload of a 900-1024-tile pack is 7-8 chunks over 50-130 ms. GPU, in-run A/B (ACZ_TERRAIN_TEXPACK_AB=30, exclusive 4x, the user's settings, cockpit, head 20 deg down, governor off, 2 runs): M2 30 m +0.021 / +0.022 ms per stereo frame, M3 40 m +0.019 / +0.022, M4 over the sea -0.003 / -0.002 (~0.04 ms on the headset path). Near-ground materials (ACZ_TERRAIN_MATERIALS) still classify by the 2006 texel and modulate the pack's colour; the shader water uses the pack's colour as its base. Exact image A/B: `PS2_PERF_AB=1 PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=texpack`. Shading only, collision unchanged; off at start: no hook, no images, no variant 2x M2: 722 / 637 of 917,504 px differ from the main build, tree-vs-tree noise 640. Headset untested. `x4` (gr_mush 2026-10-28, bug #183: M8 low over grass in rain "the ground like mush"; ENHANCEMENTS GROUND TEXTURES: REAL 4X; off unless chosen): a 4x pack, 256 x 256 tiles (1.33 m texels), made by tools/terrain/t5_pack4.py -- 4xLSDIRplusN's own 4x output (the crisp pack's model; CC-BY-4.0) in each tile's 3 x 3 world neighbourhoods, the low band (gauss 4 px) from a bicubic 4x of the 2006 texels, luma detail soft-limited to +-25 levels, chroma detail x0.7, back-projected with a bicubic residual (no 4-texel lattice) and rounded in two exact stages: its level 1 is an exact 2x and its level 2 the 2006 tile bit for bit. Within ~0.5 km the photo's soft 5 m blobs (34 px per 2006 texel at 100 m on the 4x simulator eye) become texture of grass, bushes and soil at 1-5 m; beyond ~1 km it is the same as the 2x packs. Same-frame A/B against the 2006 texture (PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=texpack, exclusive 4x, the user's settings, head 20 deg down; band energies of the luma, fine |Y - box3| / mid |box3 - box9|): M8 at 40 m, ground 150 / 200 / 300-800 m: mid x1.34 / x1.43 / x1.36-1.39, fine up to x1.59 (faithful at the same pose: x1.05 / x1.19 / x1.21-1.22); M8 at 250 m, 500 m-1.5 km: mid x1.30-1.81 (faithful x1.04-1.31); M2 at 100 m, 200-500 m: x1.31-1.48; mean luma within 0.6 levels, eyes identical. The 2x packs leave the ground below ~150 m as it was (x1.00-1.05). The renderer reads the tile side from the pack folder's first sheet at start (8192 wide = 256): 1024 layers x 9 levels = 341 MiB of VRAM and the same host staging (2x packs: 85), 32 layers a frame by default (ACZ_TERRAIN_TEXPACK_CHUNK). ### Native renderer (VU1 programs as GPU meshes)

On Zero the native VU1 path is opt-in: without `PS2_RN_VP` set, `zero_vr.c` turns it off.

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_RN_VP` | Zero: off (the Quest build's android_main: `1`); AC5: on | any non-`0` = native, `verify`, `0` = off | [experimental] Run the PS2 vector-unit programs natively as GPU meshes instead of emulating VU1; `verify` compares against VU1 | @@PS2_RN_VP@@ |
| `PS2_RN_VP_<PROG>` | on | `0` | Turn one native program off; PROG = `MODEL`, `PART`, `SHADOW`, `SKINNED`, `AIRCRAFT`, `FLAT`, `TERRAIN`, `DETAIL`, `LOADMAP`, `LIT`, `FX1`, `RAIN`, `FX2`, `TREES` | @@LINE:runtime/src/rn/rn_vp.c:const char *v = getenv(key)@@ |
| `PS2_RN_MESH` | on | `0` | Native programs hand the GPU meshes; `0` makes them emit GS packets | @@PS2_RN_MESH@@ |
| `PS2_RN_SHADOW_MESH` | on | `0` | The shadow program emits meshes too | @@PS2_RN_SHADOW_MESH@@ |
| `PS2_RN_MESH_MAT` | on | `0` | Meshes use their own fragment shader (`mesh.frag`); `0` keeps `gs.frag` for all | @@PS2_RN_MESH_MAT@@ |
| `PS2_RN_TEX` | on | `0` | Native mesh textures decoded from the recorded uploads instead of GS memory | @@PS2_RN_TEX@@ |
| `PS2_RN_TEX_VERIFY` | off | non-0 | [debug] Decode from the upload records and compare with the GS decode, logging mismatches | @@PS2_RN_TEX_VERIFY@@ |
| `PS2_RN_TEX_LOG_COPY` | off | any | [debug] Log the first 40 local-to-local VRAM copies | @@PS2_RN_TEX_LOG_COPY@@ |
| `PS2_RN_FXDBG` | `0` | N | [debug] Log the next N fx2 ribbon triangles | @@PS2_RN_FXDBG@@ |
| `PS2_RN_DUMP` | off | file path | [debug] Dump one field of the graphics stream to that file | @@PS2_RN_DUMP@@ |
| `PS2_RN_DUMP_FIELD` | `10` | field number (`0` = from the start) | Which field `PS2_RN_DUMP` writes | @@PS2_RN_DUMP_FIELD@@ |
| `PS2_MESH_BEHIND_Z` | on | `0` | Native meshes (bug #93, 2026-10-23): a vertex behind the eye keeps its homogeneous GS depth (linear in clip space) instead of 0, so a triangle the GPU clips at the eye plane gets its true depth. `0` = as before: a triangle reaching behind the eye had its depth pulled toward the far end over its near part, and M2's airfield -- big blended ground quads (runway, aprons, grass) drawn over the terrain -- lost the depth test wherever a quad reached behind the eye: shown when the head looked across it, gone (the terrain photo instead) when it looked along it (the user's "I turn my head and the texture changes", "I see through the textures"; on the roll at a fixed head 0.07-6.6 % of the eye's pixels came and went). Same-frame A/B M3 low flight: 0.00-0.03 % px > 8 (cloud noise only). GPU, exclusive 4x in-run A/B: M2 take-off roll -0.10 / -0.11 ms, M3 40 m +0.01 ms per stereo frame. PS2_MESH_BEHIND_Z_AB, PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=behindz | @@PS2_MESH_BEHIND_Z@@ |

On: the EE's vblank polling blocks on an event (PS2_PERF_EE_IDLE=1), clamp(P - 4, 0, 3) texture decode pool helpers (PS2_PERF_TEX_POOL: 2 at P = 6, 1 at 5, 0 at <= 4) that spin 50 us (PS2_PERF_TEX_POOL_SPIN), the EE rings graphics stage 1 every 64 KB (PS2_GFXQ_DOORBELL), and both graphics stages, the renderer and the pool run one priority level above the EE (PS2_THREAD_POLICY_PRIO); each of those envs, when set, wins. Forced on the full 12900K (exclusive): process 30.2 -> 15.0 (-15.2 +- 0.6), EE thread 16.73 -> 4.23, EE work -0.39 +- 0.04, stage 1 -0.31 +- 0.01, list published +0.021 +- 0.002 (p99 +0.053 +- 0.012), vblank -> polling EE mean 0.7 -> 13 us, p99 7 -> 54 us. The log line `threads: spin-free thread policy ...` names the decision and P at start; `threads-cpu:` lines (PS2_SPEED_LOG) give each thread role's CPU per field. What the headset gets is not in the eye dumps (they read the render target): checked by the shared copy code and sync validation (no new message). `0` = per eye; in-run A/B PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=eyepair | @@PS2_PERF_EYE_COPY_PAIR@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_CLOUD_BARRIERS` | on | `0` | (perf4_passes 2026-11-03) At our clouds' split points, barriers that follow each other with no command between them go to the GPU in one call: the depth's transition with the memory barrier before our hooks, and after the composite its colour barrier with the depth's transition back (one dependency info holding both: the same dependencies). Cloud barrier calls per frame (census) M3 31.8 -> 27.8, M18 26.3 -> 22.9. `0` = separate calls | @@PS2_PERF_CLOUD_BARRIERS@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_WINDOW_RATE` | `game` (play_zero_desktop.sh `record`: `full`) | `game`, `full` (or `0`), `late` (test: every frame, in-between frames take their image late) | (perf6_renderer 2026-11-03, R3) While the headset sets the pace and smooth motion draws frames between game frames, those in-between frames neither acquire, draw nor present the desktop window (present_frame + vkQueuePresentKHR, MAILBOX): the window shows the game frames, at the game's rate (before: every attempt, 120 a second at 120 Hz onto a 60 Hz desktop, half of them never seen). The headset's images are recorded and copied before the window pass and read nothing of it: unchanged. Kept every frame: ACZ_REC_CLEAN / ACZ_REC_CINE / ACZ_REC_EXACT sessions, the launcher's `record` word (OBS captures the window), the F4 menu open, PS2_DUMP_SWAP; a frame that needs the window image after all (not drawn as head-tracked stereo: a blank display, an overlay composite) acquires it late, before its window pass. The window's FPS counter keeps counting every shown frame (ps2_vk_window_fps). In-run A/B (exclusive 4x, sim 90 Hz, user settings, PS2_PERF_WINDOW_RATE_AB=60): renderer CPU per in-between attempt M3 -0.243 +- 0.015 ms, M1 -0.166 +- 0.011, M18 -0.154 +- 0.011; per game frame +0.021 +- 0.021, +0.028 +- 0.025, +0.055 +- 0.017; a 120 Hz field (one of each) -0.222 +- 0.034, -0.138 +- 0.033, -0.099 +- 0.027; GPU per in-between frame -0.032 +- 0.005, -0.034 +- 0.021, -0.036 +- 0.016 (the test's 1280x896 hidden window; a larger window saves more), game frames unchanged. | `PS2_PERF_FRAME_POOLS` | on | `0` | (perf6_renderer 2026-11-03, R4) Each frame in flight records into command buffers of its own pool (TRANSIENT, no RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT), reset whole with vkResetCommandPool once its fence has passed, instead of a vkResetCommandBuffer per buffer (the frame's and each early-submitted part's) from one shared resettable pool -- Khronos' command_buffer_usage advice for mobile drivers (the Quest port); the same commands are recorded. The resets' host time (exclusive 4x M3): 13.5-14.8 -> 6.1-7.5 us a frame (3.33 buffer resets -> 1 pool reset); ~0 of the renderer's CPU on NVIDIA. The `vk: command buffer resets` line (PS2_SPEED_LOG) gives the resets' host time a frame. `0` = one shared pool as before | @@PS2_PERF_FRAME_POOLS@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_RT_FIT` | on | `0` | (perf6_renderer 2026-11-04) The game's off-screen target slots right-sized: each slot's colour + depth images (two layers in multiview, and its snapshot) cover what its draws write (each draw's scissor clipped to its vertices' box) and what its samplers can reach (GS sprite quads: the coordinates at the pixels each quad covers; triangles: at the vertices; by wrap mode), + 8 PS2 px, instead of the whole rt_w x rt_h (58.7 MB a slot at 4x). Exact: the viewport stays the whole target, scissors and the render area are clipped to the images (no draw has a pixel outside them); gs.frag's integer texel paths (point, repeat, region repeat) read the same texels, a repeat's neighbour under 0 that wraps to the texture's last texel reads the same texel or 0 in both (the extent is chosen so), and they keep img_size = the target's size (`own`); slots read through the normalised path (bilinear with clamp / region clamp) keep the axis's full size unless that is a power of two (the 512 width in flight), then full size / 2^k, byte-identical in replays (free sizes, and 640 / 2^k with 448 / 2^k, differed in 40-240 of 3.7 M pixels, mostly by 1 level, a few by up to 53); a slot's first rendering clears it to 0 as before. Full size, sticky: the scene, the displayed slot, RT_MFD; a slot drawn by an AC5 native pass, a colour-clamp pass or a cockpit / HUD draw; sampled by a native mesh, an AC5 native pass or as depth; the depth target of a full-size slot. Off at upscale 1, with ACZ_REC_CLEAN / ACZ_REC_CINE (private copies) and ACZ_VR_GOV_OFFRT_SCALE=1. A slot that needs more grows at a game frame's start (device idle once, content copied 1:1, the rest cleared to 0, `rt-fit: slot N grows` lines); never shrinks within a session, except when the target size changes. VRAM of the off-screen slots and their snapshots, VR 2 layers (extents do not depend on the upscale), full -> right-sized: M4 224 -> 97 MB at 2x, 896 -> 388 at 4x; M1 266 -> 92, 1064 -> 366; M3 210 -> 99, 840 -> 395 (exclusive 4x run); M18 196 -> 42, 784 -> 170 (a 5-min soak: 210 -> 77 at 2x), i.e. -111..-175 MB at 2x, -250..-393 at 3x, -445..-698 at 4x. gsreplay final images byte-identical in 20 of 20 comparisons (5 captures: M2 intro, M2, M3, M14 sea, op_threads'; at 150 fields with the replay's 640 width, at 270 / 330 / 390 at the flight's 512), controls too. Renderer: the plan 20-40 us a game frame, 0-3 growths a mission (1-7 ms each with the device idle). `0` = full-size slots as before | @@PS2_PERF_RT_FIT@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_GS_SPLIT` | on | `0` | (fq_opt 2026-10-26) gs.frag (every GS draw of the game, its local-read variant too) specialised: draws whose fragment flags cannot take the target-marker paths (bit 31 clear: everything but the HUD's target boxes drawn sharp, ACZ_VR_MARKER_SHARP) get pipelines without marker_lines / marker_shape (constant 0 GS_MARKER = 0); the others ask for pipeline key bit 57, the whole shader as before. The marker code's 36 + 16 + 16 local values set the whole shader's register count: pipeline statistics 72 registers (28 warps an SM) -> 32-36 (48 warps), binary 135 -> 30 KB. The same code runs for every draw. Same-frame A/B `PS2_PERF_AB=1 PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=gssplit` 0 px in all 32 game-frame eye images (M2, M4, M12; our clouds, shader water, immersion off, M12 also eye adaptation); in-between frames at their control floor; in-run A/B `PS2_PASS_AB=60 PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=gssplit` M4 MiG-29A -0.119 +- 0.008 ms per stereo frame (3 lines), M2 Su-27 -0.129 +- 0.006 (5 lines); latency -0.12. The target boxes' states are new pipeline keys: until the keys file has them (the first session after the update, saved 20 s after they appear) each is built on demand when the boxes first show, ~7-10 ms once per state. `0` = every GS draw with the whole shader, as before | @@PS2_PERF_GS_SPLIT@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_TERRAIN_ZCULL` | on | `0` | (perf5_terrain 2026-11-04) The native terrain's overlay passes (block program 1, passes 1-3: the game's two detail textures and its world-XZ layer, the drifting cloud-shadow pattern it draws into its own render target each frame) blend Cd - Cs x FIX (GS 0x162, FIX 128) with MODULATE, no fog: where their vertex colour is 0 (beyond the game's detail fade, passes 1-2; the fog value 0, pass 3) they leave the frame exactly as it is. On: every native mesh draws with mesh.vert's variant mesh_zc*.vert (-DZCULL: one vertex program for all the terrain's passes, as before), and a draw marked by push-constant bit 1 << 27 (ps2_video.c tzc_gate: D = Cd, A / B = Cs and 0, blending on; no depth, alpha or float-target write; not the channel shuffle; no debug colour) culls the triangles whose three vertices give the texture function rgb 0 (gl_CullDistance, which never clips a triangle that keeps one vertex). Fragment census (PS2_TERRAIN_ZCENSUS, light 2x, the user's settings, median and range of 10-s windows): vertex-colour-0 share of pass 1 M3 7 % (6-11), M2 6 % (2-11), M4 3 % (0-100), M18 99 % (91-100), M1 97 % (43-100); of pass 3 (the layer: M3, M4, M14) M3 1.5 % (1.1-1.8), M4 0.9 % (0.2-1.4); with the cull on 0-0.02 %, ~1,050 draws a frame marked in M3. Pass 2 (M4, M18, M14) has no alpha test and writes alpha, so the gate leaves it. GPU (exclusive 4x, the user's settings, governor off, PS2_BENCH_REPEAT=2, layered, in-run A/B in 60-frame blocks, mean +- SE over block pairs, per game frame = two drawings): M3 -0.249 +- 0.037 ms (92 pairs; before the rebase -0.250 +- 0.037; the marks alone, the same vertex program in both arms, -0.237 +- 0.037), M18 -0.058 +- 0.030 (50), M4 -0.028 +- 0.037 (88), M2 -0.023 +- 0.025 (84), M1 -0.062 +- 0.028 (91); in-between frames unchanged (M3 -0.004 +- 0.010). Under layered that is one drawing per 120 Hz pair: M3 -0.12 ms (headset, x1.75 estimated, ~-0.22). Exact: same-frame PS2_PERF_AB_FLIP=terrzc (the re-draw with mesh.vert itself and no marks; 2x, immersion and our clouds off, the old program's pipelines built ahead: on-demand builds inside the re-draw stall it, and time-driven cockpit effects then differ) M3 and M1 16 of 16 eye images byte-identical (M3 at upscale 4: 12 of 12); M2 13 of 14, M18 14 of 16, M4 11 of 16, the rest on the image border (row 0 of the sky, last column) or in small cockpit spots, the kinds PS2_PERF_AB=2 shows with nothing flipped; gsreplay at 4x on / off byte-identical (M14 at fields 150 and 300; M2 at 150; M2 at 300 synchronously 8 of 8, with PS2_REPLAY_ASYNC=1 2 of 14 on-runs and 0 of 14 off-runs gave a second image, not explained). Needs shaderCullDistance (else off, logged). `0` = mesh.vert as before; in-run A/B PS2_PASS_AB_WHAT=terrzc (with PS2_TERRAIN_ZCULL_AB_MARKS=1: the marks alone) | @@PS2_PERF_TERRAIN_ZCULL@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_GPU_BOOST` | on | `0` | NVIDIA: keep the GPU clocks up (VK_NV_low_latency2 `lowLatencyBoost` on the window swapchain; the low-latency sleep mode stays off, the pacing stays xrWaitFrame's). The driver otherwise drops to P3 (memory 10501 -> 5001 MHz) whenever our 30-45 % load allows it: in a level M3 flight every 2 s for 0.5 s with +1.0 ms on the frame of each switch, for 30 s at a time in an M2 flight (frames +24 %), and after the pause menu, the loading screens or other light phases the first 0.5-0.75 s of flight run at 830-950 MHz (4.7-6.6 ms frames instead of 3.8). Simulator M3: in-run A/B (PS2_PERF_GPU_BOOST_AB=900, 8 block pairs) GPU mean -0.26 +- 0.12 ms, p99 -0.60 +- 0.10, block max -0.66 +- 0.09, frames over 4.76 ms 0.35 % -> 0, latency -0.27 +- 0.11 ms, P-state changes 24 -> 0; three pause/resume cycles: first second after a resume mean 4.69 -> 3.70 ms, p99 7.25 -> 4.21, flight max 7.55 -> 4.59 ms. Same commands (identical images), host times unchanged, ~+10 W GPU power. No effect without the extension. `0` = the driver's own clock policy (as before) | @@PS2_PERF_GPU_BOOST@@ |
| `PS2_PERF_EARLY_DEFER` | off | `1` | Bug #89 (fx_pacing, 2026-10-23): frames recorded before xrWaitFrame (PS2_PERF_RECORD_EARLY) keep their GPU submissions until the wait returns (the parts are ended and held, then submitted in order; the same command buffers): the recording stays off the critical path, but the GPU starts every frame -- game or in-between -- at the frame start, as it did before PS2_PERF_RECORD_EARLY, so the runtime's frame timing sees frames of one shape. The user's 10-23 headset sessions with RECORD_EARLY=1 (game frames: GPU work before the wait, ~0.1 ms after it; in-between frames: 1.1 ms of recording + the GPU after it): the predicted display time skipped a refresh on 52 % of the waits in 5-s windows with GPU < 3 ms, 26 % at 3.5-4, 5.6 % at 5-6 ms (M2 29.5 %, M3 11.1 %, M4 3.8 %), and the Link stats lost app frames 1:1 with the skips beyond the 10-22 baseline (2583-3483 a minute in M2 vs ~1200 on 10-22). Identical images (same commands). Cost: it gives the latency back -- simulator (exclusive 4x, M2 take-off, 2 runs, in-run A/B): game frames' latency (wait's end -> GPU done) 0.39-0.40 ms -> 4.21-4.35 (RECORD_EARLY=0: 4.48-4.55), in-between frames 4.4-4.6 either way, GPU unchanged; with RECORD_EARLY=2 both kinds 0.39-0.42 ms without it, 4.26-4.45 with it. Headset A/B: PS2_REC_AB=600 PS2_REC_AB_FLIP=p2,+df,++p3 (xr-pace lines per configuration) | @@PS2_PERF_EARLY_DEFER@@ |

## Profiling and diagnostics

### Timing and profiling

| Variable | Default | Values | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PS2_SPEED_LOG` | off | non-0 | CPU/GPU timing windows every 5 s (`gpu-speed: dt=...`), per-frame Vulkan call counts, pipeline compile times; in VR the `xr-pace:` lines (headset frame pacing: display-time steps by frame kind, cadence, in-between alpha, motion evenness, the runtime's dropped frames; per configuration every 30 s in an in-run A/B; PS2_XR_PACE_CSV); since perf6_threads also `speed: EE -> stage 1:` (stage 1's real wake-ups per field, the EE's ms in the signal path, the doorbell), `threads-cpu:` (CPU ms per field of every EE guest thread, stage 1, stage 2, the renderer, the pool helpers and the process, QueryThreadCycleTime) and `kernel: vblank -> the polling EE` (the vblank wake latency: mean, p50, p99, max; EE idle waits and their 1 ms timeouts) | @@PS2_SPEED_LOG@@ |
| `PS2_GPU_CLASSES` | off | any (flat and multiview); `2` = pass level | GPU time per draw class (native meshes, GS 3D, DATE, cockpit, ...); with PS2_GPU_TRACE also per frame. A timestamp at every class change (~2-3.5 us each, ~1,600 a frame in the M2 intro): never compare GPU totals with it on (nx_census). `2` (fq_opt 2026-10-26): pass level only -- every game draw counts as one class ("GS 3D opaque" = the game's draws), so a frame takes a stamp only where one of our passes starts or ends (~20-40 a frame; M2 flight +0.03-0.1 ms): the split of our own passes, with extra classes "cockpit glass", "cloud far update (early)", "frame setup before the draws", "frame setup: masks and targets", "frame setup: the draw list" | @@PS2_GPU_CLASSES@@ |
| `PS2_GPU_DRAWS` | off | any (flat only) | Every 300th frame, time each draw and log the 20 most expensive | @@PS2_GPU_DRAWS@@ |
| `PS2_DEBUG_PIPE_STATS` | off | `1` | [diagnostic] (fq_opt 2026-10-26) VK_KHR_pipeline_executable_properties: every graphics and compute pipeline made from then on logs its shaders' driver statistics (`pipe-stats:` lines: shader files, stage, register count, binary size, stack, ...): what limits a shader's occupancy (65536 registers an SM: 96 registers = 21 warps, 72 = 28, 56 = 36, <= 40 = 48). Pipelines are made with VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_CAPTURE_STATISTICS_BIT_KHR then, so the pipeline cache misses for them | @@PS2_DEBUG_PIPE_STATS@@ |
| `PS2_LOG_FPS` | off | any | Log the game's frame rate (fields with a new scene) every 600 fields | @@PS2_LOG_FPS@@ |
| `PS2_PROFILE_PHASES` | off | non-0 | Per-phase host time report at exit; with PS2_SPEED_LOG one report per 5 s window (the exit report then covers the last window) | @@PS2_PROFILE_PHASES@@ |
| `PS2_THREAD_PROF` | off | path | [diagnostic] Timeline of the frame pipeline, one CSV line per event (type,t_ns,a,b,c; CLOCK_MONOTONIC ns): vblank, EE queues a field / starts waiting, graphics worker first record / field done / published (busy, E-core and CPU time per field), list published / taken by the renderer, xrWaitFrame returned, final submission, GPU done, A/B blocks; written by a background thread every 0.25 s. `tools/perf/thread_timeline.py` rebuilds each field's path EE -> worker -> renderer -> GPU (stage times, lag, slack, attempts on screen, A/B by block). Since perf4_timeline (2026-11-03) also event 22 per renderer attempt (its stages in microseconds: fence, collect + window acquire, before the wait, xrWaitFrame + xrBeginFrame, recording, vkQueueSubmit, xrEndFrame, the rest), 23 per frame (the GPU's first timestamp on the host clock and its busy time) and 24 (PS2_VK_CENSUS_AB blocks): `tools/perf/frame_timeline.py PREFIX` joins PREFIX.tl.csv with PS2_GPU_TRACE (PREFIX.gpu.csv) and PS2_XR_PACE_CSV (PREFIX.pace.csv) into one row per game / in-between frame (PREFIX.frames.csv) and names the stage that blew the worst 1 % of the frames per scene (latency, cadence, field-to-GPU). With PS2_SPEED_LOG also a `threads:` line every 5 s: per hot thread the share of its run time on E-cores, on the favoured cores, and on a physical core shared with another hot thread | @@PS2_THREAD_PROF@@ |
| `PS2_VK_CENSUS` | off | `1` (a window every 30 s), N >= 5 (seconds) | [diagnostic] (perf4_timeline 2026-11-03; runtime/include/ps2_vkcen.h, runtime/src/ps2_vkcen.c) The Vulkan command census of every recorded frame, split by the part of the frame that recorded it, and the pass census. The renderer's files (ps2_video.c, ps2_clouds*.c, ps2_xr.c) redirect their vkCmd* calls through a counter: per part (the GPU classes of PS2_GPU_CLASSES: the game's draws by class, the HUD (xr class 2), the cockpit model / glass / composite / sun shadow / mirrors, our clouds, edge AA, the eye copies, the frame setup and uploads; set at the same pass stamps whether the class timer runs or not) and frame kind (game / in-between / other): begin-rendering, barrier calls and images, pipeline binds, descriptor sets, push constants, draws, dispatches, copies, clears, dynamic state sets; and every begin-rendering with the end-rendering before it (why the pass starts: a target switch, a snapshot copy, an early-submission split, one of our passes), every barrier (layout change, ALL_COMMANDS, BY_REGION, inside a pass), copy and clear with its call site and the caller of its function. Logged every window as `vk-census` lines (per counted frame, game / in-between); per frame totals into PS2_GPU_TRACE's `cen_*` columns. `tools/perf/vk_census.py LOG --exe build/zero/ac5.exe` pools the windows, groups the parts and names the reasons. PS2_BENCH_REPEAT's extra drawings are not counted. Cost (exclusive 4x M3, the scene with the most calls, ~12,600 counted calls a frame; in-run A/B PS2_VK_CENSUS_AB=60, 71 block pairs): recording +0.029 +- 0.009 ms per frame, the renderer's own stages incl. the fold +0.032 +- 0.013. Off: one predictable branch per redirected call | @@PS2_VK_CENSUS@@ |
| `PS2_VK_CENSUS_EVERY` | `1` | K | [diagnostic] With PS2_VK_CENSUS: only every K-th frame is counted (the census' cost / K; an odd K at 120 Hz, where game and in-between frames alternate, or one kind is never counted) | @@PS2_VK_CENSUS_EVERY@@ |
| `PS2_QUEST_CENSUS` | off | CSV path | [diagnostic] TEST-ONLY (quest_s1 2026-11-07, the Quest port's stage S1; needs PS2_VK_CENSUS) The faithful frame's census per counted frame: one CSV line per counted census frame -- the census totals (begin-rendering, barrier calls / images, pipelines, descriptor sets, push constants, draws, dispatches, copies, clears, dynamic state) and per part group (native meshes / the game's GS-path draws / the HUD / our passes / frame setup); the game's draw records issued (native mesh, GS path, native 2D / sun, fast clears); texture uploads by source (GS decodes, their replacement images, native regions of GS decodes, native textures from the upload records, other native: count, KB) with the repeats (the same contents -- key, hash, size -- uploaded before in the session, by distance <= 10 / 60 / 600 frames / older); target snapshot copies (target_snapshot_need: self-read / DATE fallback / our passes reading a target: calls, copies, area in target pixels x layers, region-only copies). Every PS2_QUEST_CENSUS_EVERY counted game frames `qcen-sig:` log lines: the GS-path draw records of game frames by state signature (draw class, xr class, target, texture source atlas / target / self, blend, alpha test, DATE, z, topology, fast clear, FBA, fog, colour clip, channel shuffle) per frame; every 600 fields `qcen-gsdec:` lines (ps2_gs.c): the direct GS decodes that make a new version of an address decoded before, with how many of their VRAM pages and whether their palette changed since the previous version (what a page-granular upload of the indexed data would move instead of the whole decoded image). With it on, native-mesh draws count in the census part `native meshes` whatever their class (native DATE / self-read draws too), so the part `DATE` holds the GS path's DATE draws only. Tools in a private script (qc_table.py, qsig_pool.py). Off (unset): one load of a static int per hook | @@PS2_QUEST_CENSUS@@ |
| `PS2_QUEST_CENSUS_EVERY` | `600` | N (counted game frames) | [diagnostic] TEST-ONLY With PS2_QUEST_CENSUS: how often the `qcen-sig:` signature lines are logged | @@PS2_QUEST_CENSUS_EVERY@@ |
| `PS2_QUEST_SKIP` | off | `k=v,k=v[;k=v,...]` (keys `rt`, `texrt`, `tme`, `fst`, `abe`, `abcd` (four digits A B C D), `ztst`, `zw`, `date`, `topo`, `fbmsk` (hex), `self`) | [debug] TEST-ONLY (quest_s1 2026-11-07; wrong images on purpose) GS-path draws (ps2_vk_draw) whose state matches every k=v of any spec (up to 8 specs) are dropped, to see in the eye dumps what a draw kind is (`texrt` = render-target slot + 1, as in PS2_DUMP_DRAWS). `texrt=7` in M3 = the ground vegetation impostors | @@PS2_QUEST_SKIP@@ |
| `PS2_MERGE_CENSUS` | off | `1` (a window every 10 s), N >= 5 (seconds) | [diagnostic] (perf5_merge 2026-11-03) Which of the game's draws could be merged: for the draws of each frame's own pass (not the PS2_BENCH_REPEAT drawings or re-draws; our passes and the cockpit model are not in the draw list), by population (native meshes of the world = xr class 1, other native meshes, GS draws), what separates each draw from the one recorded just before it -- a target / pass start, a barrier or snapshot, a pipeline bind, a descriptor-set bind, dynamic state, the scissor, other state (viewport, blend constants, vertex / index buffers), a change of kind, the push constants (and which fields), only the push constants' mesh block index (the two 480-byte blocks equal or not), or nothing. `merge-census:` lines per frame kind: draws per frame, how many would be left if every candidate merged (X1 one draw as it is; X2 with re-based indices; X3 one multi-draw with a per-draw block index) and ABAB (the draw's state equals the one two before, not the one before: interleaved passes a pass-major reorder could join); and the native terrain's passes 1-2 (detail textures: how many are wholly beyond their fade distance, i.e. draw colour 0) and pass 3 (the world-XZ layer) with their states. Game frames, light runs, the user's settings, layered default: M3 J35J 2,246 draws (native world 2,068, mean 22.8 indices) -> X1 2,246 / X2 2,151 / X3 2,104, ABAB 985 (91 % of the native world draws follow a descriptor-set bind: each terrain patch draws its atlas pass and its world-XZ layer pass alternately, ~1,000 patches); M1 overcast 1,441 -> 1,441 / 1,288 / 1,275 (push constants: the same atlas, another clamp rectangle); M18 630 -> 629 / 482 / 470; M2 take-off 1,570 -> 1,570 / 1,173 / 1,119. M3 terrain: passes 1-2 50-64 draws a frame (21-37 wholly faded), pass 3 970-1,030; all blend 0x162 (Cd - Cs x FIX), FIX 128, depth key 0x00A (no z or alpha write); M1 at altitude 45 detail draws, 44 wholly faded. Class timers off (their stamps sit between the draws). `python -I tools/perf/merge_census.py LOG` pools the windows | @@PS2_MERGE_CENSUS@@ |
| `PS2_TERRAIN_ZCENSUS` | off | N (seconds between log lines) | [diagnostic] (perf5_terrain 2026-11-04) The native terrain's draws take the fragment shaders' census variants (mesh_zcen*, gs_zcen*: terrain_zcensus.glsl; needs fragmentStoresAndAtomics), which count each pass's fragments atomically into two reserved mesh blocks (the frame's arena stops below them): `terrain-zc:` lines per pass (0 the atlas -- only patches drawn by the plain mesh.frag --, 1-2 the detail textures, 3 the world-XZ layer): fragments a frame (both eyes; helpers not counted), the share that reached the output (DATE / alpha test), and of those the vertex colour rgb 0, the texel rgb 0, the exact no-ops (output rgb 0: the blend leaves the target as it is), the texel 0 under a non-zero colour, the no-ops by the blend's rounding only (output under half a level); and the overlay draws marked for PS2_PERF_TERRAIN_ZCULL. Light runs at 2x, the user's settings, cull off, median (range) of the 10-s windows: M3 pass 3 779 k fragments a frame, texel 0 83 % (25-98), colour 0 1.5 % (1.1-1.8), no-op by rounding only 0.7 % (0.2-2.8); pass 1 827 k, colour 0 7 % (6-11); M4 pass 3 777 k, texel 0 96 % (38-99.8); M2 no pass 3, pass 1 1,058 k, colour 0 6 % (2-11); M18 no pass 3, pass 1 378 k, colour 0 99 % (91-100); M1 no pass 3, pass 1 360 k, colour 0 97 % (43-100).
